Sub-Awardee Name: THE ADMINISTRATORS OF TULANE EDUCATIONAL FUND
Sub-Award Description:
THE WORK FOR EACH TRAINING CYCLE COHORT WOULD BE ONE MONTH:
1. ATTENDANCE BY ONE FACULTY MEMBER OF ONE HOUR ONBOARDING KICK-OFF WEBINAR FOR ATTENDEES.
2. REVIEW BY A MINIMUM OF THREE FACULTY MEMBERS OF WORKSHEETS SUBMITTED ON A WEEKLY BASIS BY EACH OF THE 15 PRACTICES THAT ARE A PART OF THE COHORT.
3. INTERACTION BY FACULTY MEMBERS WITH PRACTICES ON A WEEKLY BASIS VIA THE LIST-SERV PROVIDED OR VIA PHONE/EMAIL TO ANSWER QUESTIONS ABOUT THE FUNDAMENTALS OF TEAMSTEPPS.
4. ATTENDANCE BY FACULTY ON A WEEKLY CALL WITH HRET DURING THE MONTH OF THE TRAINING TO DISCUSS THE PRACTICES AND THE TRENDS WE ARE SEEING FROM THEIR WORKSHEETS.
5. CREATION OF A MINIMUM OF THREE COACHING SCENARIOS FOR ATTENDEES TO PRACTICE IN-PERSON BASED ON THE INFORMATION BEING SUBMITTED ON THE WORKSHEETS OR THE LIST-SERV.
6. TEACHING A ONE DAY COURSE IN PERSON TO ATTENDEES BY A MINIMUM OF THREE FACULTY MEMBERS.  THIS COURSE WILL BE BASED ON TEAMSTEPPS IN PRIMARY CARE MATERIAL CREATED BY HRET.
7. INTERACTION WITH PRACTICES FOR 2 MORE WEEKS ONLINE AFTER THE TRAINING VIA LIST-SERV.

Awarding Sub Agency: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality

Sub-Award Description:
"OBJECTIVE 1:  DEVELOPMENT AND LAUNCH OF EFFECTIVE BREAST CANCER GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY CHALLENGE. 

IN THE PROPOSED WORK, SAGE BIONETWORKS WORK WITH NCI AND NCI PRIZE ADVISORY COMMITTEE TO DEVELOP AN EFFECTIVE CHALLENGE.  THIS WORK WILL INCLUDE PREPARATION OF CHALLENGE DESCRIPTION, RULES, AND EVALUATION CRITERIA.  IN ADDITION, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL PREPARE THE CHALLENGE HUB USING THE SYNAPSE INFRASTRUCTURE FOR THE CHALLENGE, INCLUDING POSTING ALL RULES, DESCRIPTIVE INFORMATION, FAQS, AND INSTRUCTIONS FOR CHALLENGE PARTICIPATION.  SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL ALSO PROVIDE DATA SCIENTIST SUPPORT TO WORK WITH THE CHALLENGE LEADER AND OTHER DATA SCIENTISTS AS PART OF THE CHALLENGE ORGANIZATIONAL TEAM.  THE SAGE APPOINTED DATA SCIENTIST WILL HELP GUIDE THE TEAM IN CHALLENGE Â€˜BEST PRACTICESÂ€™, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO PRE-CHALLENGE DRY-RUN AND SUPPORT FOR THE SYNAPSE PLATFORM.  SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL WORK WITH NCI TO ANNOUNCE LAUNCHING OF THE CHALLENGE. 

 

OBJECTIVE 2: MANAGEMENT AND PROMOTION OF BREAST CANCER GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY CHALLENGE. 

IN THE PROPOSED WORK, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL PERFORM DISSEMINATION ACTIVITIES FOR THE CHALLENGE AND POST CHALLENGE ON THE SAGE/SYNAPSE PLATFORM.  THEY WILL DEVELOP A CHALLENGE HUB TO FACILITATE PARTICIPATION IN THE CHALLENGE.  THIS HUB WILL INCLUDE REGISTRATION AND TRACKING OF CHALLENGE PARTICIPANTS, PROVIDING SUPPORT FOR DATA ACCESS REQUESTS, SUPPORT FOR PARTICIPANTS REQARDING INQUIRES, TRANSLATION SERVICES, COMMUNITY FORUM AND MANAGEMENT OF SUBMISSIONS OF CHALLENGE SOLUTIONS. 

 

OBJECTIVE 3: EVALUATION, AWARD AND DISSEMINATION OF BREAST CANCER GENETIC EPIDEMIOLOGY CHALLENGE SOLUTIONS. 

IN THE PROPOSED WORK, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL MANAGE EVALUATIONS OF CHALLENGE SUBMISSIONS, ANNOUNCE WINNER OF THE PRIZE, PROVIDE THE CHALLENGE AWARD AND PARTICIPATE IN DISSEMINATION OF THE CHALLENG SOLUTION AND NARRATIVE DESCRIPTION OF THE CHALLENGE PROCESS.  FINALLY, SAGE BIONETWORKS WILL PROVIDE POST-CHALLENGE INFRASTRUCTURE SUPPORT BY STORING SUMMARY OF SUBMISSIONS AND SOURCE CODE, AS APPROPRIATE, FOR THE CHALLENGE. "
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

TASK G: TASK ADMINISTRATION ACTIVITIES.
TASK 1:  DEVELOP AN INNOVATION MODEL PORTFOLIO EXPANSION PLAN - PERFORM AN ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN OF THE CURRENT HEALTHCARE MARKET ON INNOVATIVE PAYMENT MODELS, IDENTIFY AND PROPOSE A LIST OF APPROPRIATE STAKEHOLDERS TO SOLICIT INPUT FOR THE MODEL PORTFOLIO EXPANSION PLAN. PARTICIPATE IN THE ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY AND DOCUMENT GAPS IN THE CURRENT CMS INNOVATION MODEL PORTFOLIO. CONTRIBUTE TO DEVELOPING A PRIORITIZATION FRAMEWORK FOR ASSESSING MODEL OPPORTUNITIES. PARTICIPATE IN THE ASSESSMENT OF INNOVATION MODEL OPPORTUNITIES ANALYSIS. DEVELOP A PRELIMINARY ASSESSMENT OF MODEL OPPORTUNITIES DOCUMENT INCORPORATING AND SYNTHESIZING INFORMATION FROM THE ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN, STAKEHOLDER INPUTS, CURRENT MODELS INVENTORY, AND THE MODEL PRIORITIZATION FRAMEWORK.
TASK 2: INNOVATION MODEL DEVELOPMENT - -SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF A MODEL CONCEPT PAPER BASED ON THE MODEL PORTFOLIO EXPANSION PLAN (TASK 1). SUPPORT THE FORMATION OF A TECHNICAL EXPERT PANEL (TEP) FOR EACH MODEL FOCUS AREA. PROVIDE INPUT AND SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE TEP MATERIALS, INCLUDING TEP FORMATION PLANS, TEP SESSION PLANS, INPUT MATERIALS FOR THE SESSIONS, AND TEP MEETING REPORTS. SUPPORT MODEL ANALYSIS AND DESIGN FOR EACH SELECTED MODEL AND DEVELOP THE MODEL DESIGN REPORTS. PROVIDE INPUT TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF INNOVATION CENTER INVESTMENT PROPOSALS (ICIP). DEVELOP SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION ON THE DATA FILE SOURCES AND DESIGN OF THE DATA ANALYTIC TOOL FOR THE ICIP DEVELOPMENT TASK. DESIGN AND EXECUTE MODEL SIMULATIONS.

Sub-Award Description: ACCORD FOLLOW-ON STUDY IS A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL FOLLOW-UP STUDY OF APPROXIMATELY 8,000 PARTICIPANTS WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED IN THE ACTION TO CONTROL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN DIABETES (ACCORD) TRIAL.  IT IS DESIGNED TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE AND CLARIFY THE LONG-TERM EFFECT OF THE ACCORTD TREATMENT STRATEGIES AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL DATA ON THE LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND DIABETIC RISK FACTORS.  ACCORD WAS A RANDOMIZED CARDIOVASCULAR CLINICAL TRIAL IN PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED FOR AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 YEARS FROM 2001 THROUGH MID-2009.  ACCORD PARTICIPANTS WHO AGREE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOW-ON STUDY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FOLLOWED THROUGH CLINIC AND PHONE VISITS FOR AN AVERAGE OF 3.5 YEARS IN THE PERIOD 2011 THROUGH 2014.  PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA.  THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT.  SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME.  LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

Sub-Award Description:
THE SICKLE CELL DISEASE TREATMENT DEMONSTRATION PROGRAM (SCDTDP) PROVIDES GRANTS TO REGIONAL NETWORKS THAT WILL WORK WITH PRIMARY CARE PRACTICES THAT TREAT SICKLE CELL DISEASE, COMPREHENSIVE SICKLE CELL DISEASE CENTERS, AND COMMUNITY-BASED SUPPORT ORGANIZATIONS TO PROVIDE COORDINATED, COMPREHENSIVE, CULTURALLY COMPETENT, AND FAMILY-CENTERED CARE TO FAMILIES WITH SICKLE CELL DISEASE.

TO ADDRESS THESE BARRIERS TO ACCESS TO SICKLE CELL DISEASE CARE, THE MATERNAL AND CHILD HEALTH BUREAU (MCHB) IS ADJUSTING THE SCDTDP TO A REGIONAL MODEL.  THE REGIONAL APPROACH HAS BEEN USED BY MCHB WITH OTHER PROGRAMS AND WILL INCREASE THE REACH OF THE PROGRAM TO PROVIDE ACCESS TO A GREATER NUMBER OF PATIENTS.

Sub-Award Description:
THE AMERICAN INSTITUTES FOR RESEARCH (AIR) HAS IN PLACE THE NECESSARY ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE AND EXPERIENCE TO COMPLETE THE WORK ASSIGNED UNDER THIS AGREEMENT. WE HAVE BUDGETED THE TASKS AS DESCRIBED BELOW TO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF THE BAYLOR COLLEGE OF MEDICINE EISENBERG CENTER (E.G., ENSURING GEOGRAPHIC DIVERSITY, AND HIGH-QUALITY RECRUITS).  WE CAN ADJUST PRODUCT TESTING OR FORMATIVE RESEARCH ACTIVITIES THROUGHOUT THE CONTRACT TO ADDRESS CHANGING NEEDS OF THE EC-BCM. 
MANAGEMENT. AIR AND BCM WILL WORK COLLABORATIVELY TO DISSEMINATE FINDINGS FROM THE EISENBERG CENTER TESTING AND FORMATIVE RESEARCH ACTIVITIES. WE HAVE BUDGETED HOURS FOR MANAGEMENT OF THE CONTRACT, WHICH INCLUDES TIME FOR MONTHLY MONITORING OF THE PROJECTÂ€™S BUDGET, COORDINATING STAFFING ACROSS PROJECT ACTIVITIES, WEEKLY MEETINGS WITH THE EISENBERG CENTER, AND INTERNAL PROJECT MEETINGS ACROSS TRANSLATION TOPICS. WHILE LEVEL OF EFFORT REMAINS ROUGHLY EQUAL ACROSS ALL YEARS FOR THIS TASK, WE ESTIMATE AN INCREASE OF ABOUT $2,800 PER YEAR FOR AIRÂ€™S ANNUAL COST OF LIVING SALARY INCREASES. 
AIR WILL CONDUCT CLINICIAN TESTING FOR SIX TRANSLATION PRODUCTS AND CONSUMER TESTING FOR SIX TRANSLATION PRODUCTS EACH YEAR. CLINICIAN TESTING INCLUDES SEVEN CLINICIAN ONE-HOUR COGNITIVE INTERVIEWS WITH FIVE GENERAL PRACTITIONERS AND TWO SPECIALISTS. CONSUMER TESTING INCLUDES NINE 90-MINUTE IN-PERSON INTERVIEWS WITH CONSUMERS AT PROFESSIONAL FACILITIES OR AN AIR OFFICE LOCATION (I.E., WASHINGTON, DC, CHAPEL HILL, NC, OR SAN MATEO, CA) 
BELOW, WE DESCRIBE OUR OVERALL PROCESS AND ASSUMPTIONS FOR THE PRODUCT TESTING AND FORMATIVE RESEARCH ACTIVITIES. THESE ASSUMPTIONS APPLY ACROSS ALL YEARS OF THE PROJECT. 
RECRUITMENT. CLINICIANS AND CONSUMERS WILL BE RECRUITED THROUGH PROFESSIONAL RECRUITMENT FIRMS, DEPENDENT ON PRODUCT TESTING LOCATION. FOR RESEARCH WITH CONSUMERS, AIR WILL OVER-RECRUIT TO OBTAIN THE DESIRED NUMBER OF RESPONDENTS (RECRUIT 12 TO GET 9). BASED ON OUR RECENT EXPERIENCES ON THE PREVIOUS CONTRACT, WE HAVE BUDGETED RECRUITMENT COSTS OF $160 FOR CONSUMERS AND $150 FOR CLINICIANS. 
DATA COLLECTION AND ANALYSIS. ALL INTERVIEWERS WILL WORK COLLABORATIVELY UNDER THE GUIDANCE OF DR. FIRMINGER TO CONDUCT THE INTERVIEWS, ANALYZE THE RESULTS, PREPARE THE TOPLINE REPORTS, AND PRESENT THE RESULTS TO THE EC-BCM. FOR THE CONSUMER RESEARCH, INTERVIEWERS AND NOTETAKERS WILL BE DETERMINED BY LOCATION AND AVAILABILITY. 
INCENTIVES. BASED ON OUR RECENT EXPERIENCES ON THE PREVIOUS CONTRACT, WE HAVE BUDGETED INCENTIVES OF $100 FOR CONSUMERS. FOR CLINICIANS, WE HAVE BUDGETED $150 INCENTIVES FOR GENERAL PRACTITIONERS AND $250 INCENTIVES FOR SPECIALISTS. WE WILL WORK WITH THE EC-BCM IF PRODUCT TRANSLATION TOPICS REQUIRE SPECIALIZED POPULATIONS THAT REQUIRE HIGHER INCENTIVES. 
TASK 8: CONSUMER AND PATIENT ACTIVATION AND ENGAGEMENT IN EHC ACTIVITIES 
AIR WILL LEAD THE EFFORTS TO ENGAGE CONSUMER AND PATIENT ORGANIZATIONS THROUGHOUT THE FIVE YEARS. 
IN YEARS 1 THROUGH 5, THE EC-BCM WILL MEET WITH AHRQ TO DISCUSS EXPECTATIONS AND POTENTIAL ENGAGEMENT ACTIVITIES; DEVELOP AN ENGAGEMENT PLAN FOR THE YEAR; MEET AND WORK WITH 15 PATIENT AND CONSUMER ORGANIZATIONS; PLAN AND FACILITATE 4 TO 5 TELECONFERENCES WITH PATIENT AND CONSUMER ORGANIZATIONS AND AHRQ STAFF; AND DISSEMINATE INFORMATION TO PATIENTS AND CONSUMERS TO HIGHLIGHT AHRQ ACTIVITIES AND ENGAGEMENT OPPORTUNITIES. IN YEAR 1, THE EC-BCM WILL RECRUIT 15 CONSUMER AND PATIENT ORGANIZATIONS; DEVELOP PROCESSES FOR MATCHING PATIENT AND CONSUMER REPRESENTATIVES WITH AHRQ AND EHC PROGRAM RESEARCH PROJECTS; ESTABLISH STANDARDIZED APPROACHES AND GUIDANCE ON HOW TO SUCCESSFULLY INVOLVE PATIENT AND CONSUMER PARTICIPANTS; DEVELOP A PASSWORD PROTECTED ONLINE RESOURCE CENTER FOR PATIENTS AND CONSUMERS ENGAGED IN SPECIFIC ACTIVITIES; CREATE AND HOST THREE MULTIMEDIA PRESENTATIONS AND ENSURE THEY ARE 508 COMPLIANT TO POST ON THE EHC WEB SITE; AND DEVELOP FEEDBACK FORMS TO COLLECT FEEDBACK ABOUT THE ENGAGEMENT PROCESS AND OUTCOMES.

Sub-Award Description:
JOHNS HOPKINS SCOPE OF WORK

A. INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES
EMERGING INSIGHT INTO TUMOR GENOMES MAKES IT CLEAR THAT CHROMOSOMAL TRANSLOCATIONS OCCUR RELATIVELY COMMONLY AND IN A NON-RANDOM FASHION (1-3). FUSION PROTEINS THAT FORM AS A RESULT OF THESE TRANSLOCATIONS TYPICALLY HAVE ALTERED FUNCTIONS RELATIVE TO THE INDIVIDUAL SOURCE PROTEINS AND, IN SOME CASES, APPEAR TO DRIVE THE MALIGNANT PHENOTYPE. SINCE THE FUSION PROTEINS ARISE DURING TUMOR DEVELOPMENT, AND ARE NOT EXPRESSED IN NORMAL TISSUES, THEY REPRESENT TUMOR-SPECIFIC ANTIGENS AND PROVIDE POTENTIAL TARGETS FOR TUMOR VACCINES. THERAPEUTIC BREAKPOINT PEPTIDE VACCINES WITH EVIDENCE OF CLINICAL ACTIVITY WERE FIRST DEVELOPED AGAINST THE BCRABL FUSIONS OBSERVED IN CML (4-6). WHILE THE SIZE OF THE TRIALS CONDUCTED HAVE BEEN MODEST AND THE EXACT CONTENT OF THE VACCINES VARIABLE, THE BODY OF THE DATA SUPPORTS THE POTENTIAL FOR CLINICAL ACTIVITY OF THE PRODUCTS.

MORE MODEST PROGRESS HAS BEEN MADE USING THERAPEUTIC BREAKPOINT VACCINES AGAINST CHARACTERISTIC FUSIONS OBSERVED IN SARCOMAS (7-9). GIVEN THAT VACCINATION AGAINST HPV, THE VIRUS THAT INDUCES CERVICAL CANCER, IS CAPABLE OF PROTECTING WOMEN FROM THE DEVELOPMENT OF CERVICAL CANCER WHEN GIVEN PRIOR TO VIRUS EXPOSURE, YET INEFFECTIVE IN THE TREATMENT SETTING AFTER THE CANCER HAS ALREADY DEVELOPED (10), BREAKPOINT VACCINES MAY ALSO BE MORE EFFECTIVE AS A PREVENTATIVE THERAPY. HOWEVER, SO FAR, NO BREAKPOINT-SPECIFIC VACCINES HAVE BEEN DEVELOPED FOR CANCER PREVENTION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT A MULTIVALENT VACCINE DIRECTED AGAINST FUSION PROTEINS OBSERVED IN SOLID TUMORS COULD GENERATE AN IMMUNE RESPONSE CAPABLE OF PREVENTING SOLID TUMORS IN HIGH-RISK GROUPS OF PATIENTS. IN ADULT SOLID TUMORS, FUSIONS INVOLVING SOME OF THE SAME AND SOME DIFFERENT SOURCE GENES AS THOSE IDENTIFIED IN SARCOMAS HAVE BEEN OBSERVED. SINCE THE SAME SET OF TRANSLOCATIONS AND CORRESPONDING FUSION PROTEINS ARE NOT OBSERVED IN ALL TUMORS OF A GIVEN HISTOLOGIC TYPE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT A STRATEGY THAT TARGETS MULTIPLE, FREQUENTLY OBSERVED FUSIONS HAS THE BEST CHANCE OF GENERATING EFFECTIVE ANTITUMOR IMMUNITY AND PROTECTION. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS STUDY IS TO DEFINE ONE OR MORE PRECLINICAL MODELS TO DEVELOP THIS APPROACH AND EVALUATE ITS POTENTIAL FOR THE PREVENTION OF SOLID TUMORS.


OBJECTIVES

1. TO IDENTIFY T CELL TARGETABLE GENE FUSION ANTIGENS EXPRESSED BY THE MURINE LEWIS LUNG CANCER AND MC38 COLON CANCER CELL LINES. 

2. TO EVALUATE THE IMMUNOGENICITY OF AN EML4-ALK GENE FUSION THAT DRIVES TUMOR DEVELOPMENT IN A TRANSGENIC
LUNG CANCER MODEL.

3. TO DEVELOP PEPTIDE AND LISTERIA-BASED IMMUNIZATION STRATEGIES FOR INDUCING ROBUST GENE FUSION-SPECIFIC
EFFECTOR T CELL RESPONSES.

4. TO EVALUATE THE PRECLINICAL EFFICACY OF GENE FUSION-SPECIFIC IMMUNIZATION STRATEGIES FOR PREVENTING TUMOR DEVELOPMENT.

Sub-Award Description:
OPTION 15A (09/15/14-02/29/16): 0258-0516-4609

THE ROLES OF SPECIFIC SIALIC ACID VARIANTS IN INFLUENZA-HOST CELL INTERACTIONS.
WE ARE FOCUSING ON BETTER UNDERSTANDING THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA VIRUSES AND DIFFERENT HOSTS BY DEFINING THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA HA AND NA AND SPECIFICALLY MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS (WITH ADDITIONAL ACETYLATIONS, HYDROXYLATIONS, AND/OR LINKAGES) DISPLAYED ON THE VARIOUS TARGET CELLS AND TISSUES FROM DIFFERENT HOSTS.  THESE LIKELY MODIFY THE SPECIFIC PROCESSES OF VIRUS CELL BINDING, INFECTION AND SHEDDING AND WILL THEREFORE ADD TO OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE VIRUS-HOST INTERACTION, AND PROVIDE INSIGHTS INTO POTENTIAL NEW INTERVENTION STRATEGIES. 
IN THE FIRST PART OF THE PROJECT WE WILL DEVELOP TOOLS FOR DETECTING THE PRESENCE OF MODIFIED FORMS OF SA ON CELLS AND TISSUES. WE WILL PREPARE PROBES FOR QUANTITATIVELY ASSAYING FOR THE PRESENCE OF NEU5AC AND NEU5GC ON CELLS AND TISSUES USING PARVOVIRUS CAPSIDS, ANTIBODIES RECOGNIZING NEU5GC, AND BACTERIAL TOXIN SUBUNITS. PROBES FOR 4-O-ACETYLATED SAS WILL BE DERIVED FROM THE MOUSE HEPATITIS VIRUS (MHV) HEMAGGLUTININ-ESTERASE (HE), AND THE MHV-S HE ESTERASE WOULD BE USED TO REMOVE THE 4-O-ACETYL GROUP FROM THE SA ON CELLS OR TISSUES. PROBES FOR 9-O-ACETYLATED SA WILL BE DERIVED FROM THE BOVINE CORONAVIRUS HE PROTEIN OR INFLUENZA C HE PROTEIN, AND ESTERASE ACTIVE FORMS WOULD BE USED AS MODIFYING ENZYMES. OTHER PROBES THAT WE WILL DEVELOP FOR THIS TESTING INCLUDE SPECIFIC INFLUENZA HA DOMAINS LINKED TO THE FC PORTION OF HUMAN IGG1.
IN THE SECOND PART OF THE PROJECT WE WILL DEFINE THE SPECIFIC SA FORMS AND LINKAGES EXPRESSED ON THE RESPIRATORY EPITHELIAL AND OTHER CELLS OF NATURAL HOSTS OF INFLUENZA, SO AS TO UNDERSTAND THE CORRELATIONS BETWEEN HA BINDING AND NA CLEAVAGE AND NATURAL VIRUS SUSCEPTIBILITY. WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE THE EXPRESSION OF THE MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS ON CELLS IN TISSUE CULTURE, AND THEN WILL TEST FOR THE EFFECTS OF SA MODIFICATIONS ON VIRUS BINDING, INFECTION, AND RELEASE, OR INTERACTIONS WITH HOST PROTEINS.

OPTION 22D (09/10/16-12/09/17): 0258-0578-4609

DR. COLIN R. PARRISH (CORNELL UNIVERSITY) WILL COORDINATE STUDIES TO DEFINE THE ROLES OF MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS (SIAS) IN CONTROLLING THE HOST RANGES AND TROPISMS OF INFLUENZA A VIRUSES. INFLUENZA VIRUSES ALL BIND AND CLEAVE SPECIFIC SIAS DURING MANY INTERACTIONS WITH THEIR HOSTS, AND IN THIS PROPOSAL THE PARRISH LABORATORY WILL DEFINE THE EXPRESSION OF MODIFIED SIA RECEPTORS, AND EXPLAIN THEIR ROLES IN THE CONTROL OF INFLUENZA VIRUS INTERACTIONS WITH HOST CELLS AND TISSUES. PRIMARY GOALS OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO PREPARE SPECIFIC PROBES THAT RECOGNIZE THE DIFFERENT MODIFIED FORMS OF SIALIC ACID THAT ARE EXPRESSED ON CELLS, AND THEN TO DEFINE THEIR EFFECTS ON VIRUS INFECTION. THE SPECIFIC PROJECT INVOLVES THE PREPARATION OF A VARIETY OF PROBES BY EXPRESSION OF PROTEINS IN BACULOVIRUS SYSTEMS WHERE THE PROTEIN IS SECRETED AND PURIFIED. THE DIFFERENT PROBES ARE BEING USED TO DETECT THE PRESENCE OF DIFFERENT MODIFIED SIALIC ACIDS ON PROTEINS, CELLS, OR TISSUES OBTAINED FROM DIFFERENT HOSTS, USING A VARIETY OF DETECTION METHODS. WE WOULD ALSO USE VARIOUS ENZYMES TO ALTER THE EXPRESSION OF DIFFERENT SIALIC ACIDS, TO MODIFY THE SIALIC ACIDS ON THE SURFACE OF CELLS, AND WOULD USE CRSP/CAS9 EDITING OF GENES IN CELLS TO ALTER THE SIALIC ACID EXPRESSION. THE MODIFIED SIALIC ACID FORMS WOULD THEN BE TESTED FOR THEIR INTERACTIONS WITH INFLUENZA VIRUSES, OR THEIR EXPRESSED PROTEINS.

DR. PARRISH WILL OVERSEE THE LOCAL MANAGEMENT OF THIS RESEARCH PROJECT AT CORNELL, AND WILL ASSIST IN THE PREPARATION OF MONTHLY, SEMI-ANNUAL, AND ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS. HE WILL ALSO OVERSEE THE WRITING OF SCIENTIFIC PUBLICATIONS DESCRIBING THE RESULTS OF THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM.

THIS WORK DIRECTLY REFLECTS BOTH THE SPECIFIC AND OVERALL GOALS OF THE CEIRS PROGRAM, AND IS HIGHLY COMPLEMENTARY TO A NUMBER OF PROJECTS WITHIN THE CEIRS NETWORK, PARTICULARLY THOSE EXAMINING THE HOST AND TISSUE TROPISMS OF THE VARIOUS INFLUENZA VIRUSES IN MAMMALS AND IN DIFFERENT AVIAN HOSTS. WE WILL GAIN A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA VIRUSES AND THEIR HOSTS BY DEFINING THE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN INFLUENZA HA AND NA AND THE SPECIFICALLY MODIFIED RECEPTORS ON HOST CELLS AND TISSUES, WHICH LIKELY CONTROL THE SPECIFIC PROCESSES OF VIRUS INFECTION OF CELLS AND TISSUES OF DIFFERENT HOSTS, INTERACTIONS WITH MUCUS, AND VIRUS SHEDDING. THE RESULTS WILL ALSO PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO POTENTIAL INTERVENTIONS

Sub-Awardee Name: THE ADMINISTRATORS OF TULANE EDUCATIONAL FUND
Sub-Award Description:
PROVIDE TEAMSTEPPS TRAINING FOR 40-50 PARTICIPANTS PER TRAINING, MAXIMUM 4 TRAININGS PER YEAR AT $16,000 PER TRAINING.
-TRAINING ARE 2 DAYS IN LENGTH
-THE DATES OF THE TRAININGS ARE DETERMINED BEFORE THE TEAMSTEPPS REBOOT MEETING
-THE CENTER WILL PROVIDE A GENERIC WELCOME LETTER TO HRET PRIOR TO THE REBOOT MEETING WHICH WILL BE SENT AUTOMATICALLY TO EACH REGISTRANT
-CENTER SHOULD FUNNEL ALL REGISTRATION QUESTIONS DIRECTLY TO HRET VIA AHRQTEAMSTEPPS@AHA.ORG
-ONSITE CENTERS SHOULD VERIFY THAT THE EMAIL ADDRESSES OF ATTENDEES PROVIDED WHEN REGISTRATION IS ACCURATE
FOR CEU'S THE CENTER MUST:
-NOTIFY ATTENDEES THAT AN EVALUATION WILL BE CIRCULATED ONE DAY POST TRAINING 
-SUBMIT A SIGN IN SHEET OF ATTENDEES TO HRET WITHIN 2 WEEK OF TRAINING
-MARK ATTENDANCE IN THE ONLINE REGISTRATION CENTER WITHIN 2 DAYS
-THE CENTER WILL CREATE NAME TAGS/TABLE TENTS BASED ON REGISTRATION INFORMATION PROVIDE BY HRET
-PROVIDE FOR ACCOMMODATING THE NEEDS OF TRAINING PARTICIPANTS WHILE ONSITE
-REPRESENTATIVES FROM THE CENTER WILL CONTRIBUTE TO TEAMSTEPPS USER LEARNING NETWORK VIA LISTSERVS AND/OR DISCUSSION FORUMS AS NECESSARY
SUPPORT NATIONAL IMPLEMENTATION SERVICES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO:
-REVIEWING OF ABSTRACTS FOR NATIONAL CONFERENCE
-PRESENTING AT THE NATIONAL CONFERENCE
-PRESENTING AT NATIONAL WEBINAR
-SERVING ON FOCUS GROUP TO PROVIDE FEEDBACK
-PROVIDING IMPLEMENTATION COACHING
-SENDING A TEAM OF THREE TO THE ANNUAL REBOOT MEETING

Sub-Award Description:
1. ENSURE THE RECRUITMENT OF AT LEAST 15 LONG TERM CARE FACILITIES THROUGHOUT THE DURATION OF THE 12 MONTH PROJECT PARTICIPATION PERIOD.
2. OBTAIN AND MAINTAIN GENERAL KNOWLEDGE OF THE PROJECT (GOALS, EXPECTATIONS, INTERVENTIONS, TIMELINES, SCHEDULES, ETC.) AND SERVE AS A LIAISON BETWEEN THE NATIONAL PROGRAM TEAM AND THE LTCFS.
3. ENCOURAGE ALL LTCF TEAM MEMBERS TO COMPLETE THE TWO SAFETY CULTURE SURVEY ADMINISTRATIONS (BASELINE AND PROJECT CLOSE), AND ASSIST WITH SAFETY CULTURE IMPROVEMENTS AND OVERCOMING PROGRAM BARRIERS BY ADOPTING TECHNIQUES DISCUSSED ON NATIONAL CONTENT CALLS RELATED TO SAFETY CULTURE.
4. MONITOR LTCF'S MONTHLY DATA REPORTS PROVIDED BY HRET, AND ADVISE LTCFS WITH OUTLIER RESULTS OR LOW DATA SUBMISSION RATES TO PARTICIPATE IN OFFICE HOURS TO IMPROVE PERFORMANCE.
5. PARTICIPATE ALONG WITH AT LEAST ONE TEAM MEMBER FROM EACH LTCF ON ALL EDUCATIONAL WEBINARS AND CONFERENCE CALLS.
6. COMMIT TO THE AHRQ'S SAFETY PROGRAM FOR LONG TERM CARE CHANGE PACKAGE INTERVENTION, WHICH INCLUDES: EVIDENCE-BASED INFECTION AND COMPLICATION PREVENTION PRACTICES; IMPROVED SAFETY CULTURE THROUGH THE ADAPTATION OF THE PROVEN SAFETY PROGRAM KNOWN AS CUSP.

THE STUDY ADDRESSES AN IMPORTANT BIOLOGIC CONCEPT, I.E. Sub-Award Description: ACCORD FOLLOW-ON STUDY IS A PROSPECTIVE, OBSERVATIONAL FOLLOW-UP STUDY OF APPROXIMATELY 8,000 PARTICIPANTS WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED IN THE ACTION TO CONTROL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK IN DIABETES (ACCORD) TRIAL.  IT IS DESIGNED TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE AND CLARIFY THE LONG-TERM EFFECT OF THE ACCORTD TREATMENT STRATEGIES AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL DATA ON THE LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND DIABETIC RISK FACTORS.  ACCORD WAS A RANDOMIZED CARDIOVASCULAR CLINICAL TRIAL IN PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED FOR AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 YEARS FROM 2001 THROUGH MID-2009.  ACCORD PARTICIPANTS WHO AGREE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOW-ON STUDY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FOLLOWED THROUGH CLINIC AND PHONE VISITS FOR AN AVERAGE OF 3.5 YEARS IN THE PERIOD 2011 THROUGH 2014.  PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA.  THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT.  SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME.  LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

Sub-Award Description:
BRIEF SUMMARY: THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS 5-YEAR FDA AWARD IS TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT STRATEGIES TO ASSESS, EVALUATE, AND MONITOR MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURE SAFETY, PERFORMANCE, AND PATIENT COMPLIANCE IN RESPONSE TO A PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCY. CLINICAL SITES FOR THE UNITED STATES CRITICAL ILLNESS AND INJURY TRIALS GROUP PROGRAM FOR EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS (USCIITG-PREP) HAVE BEEN RECRUITED TO PERFORM THIS WORK. THE WORK IS DIVIDED INTO A BASE PERIOD AND 4 ONE-YEAR OPTION PERIODS.
BASE PERIOD (YEARS 1-4): THERE ARE FOUR DELIVERABLES IDENTIFIED FOR THE BASE PERIOD:
Â€¢ IN YEAR 1, DEVELOP AN INTRAVENOUS ANTIVIRAL TREATMENT PROTOCOL TO ASSESS THE USE OF INTRAVENOUS (IV) ANTIVIRALS (E.G., IV ZANAMIVIR) UNDER AN EXPANDED ACCESS IND FOR CRITICALLY ILL PATIENTS WITH CONFIRMED INFLUENZA USING ELECTRONIC CASE REPORT FORMS (ECRFS) AND A DATA ENTRY USER MANUAL.
Â€¢ UTILIZE PRE-ESTABLISHED INFRASTRUCTURE FOR BROAD COVERAGE OF CLINICAL TRIAL SITES ACROSS THE UNITED STATES
Â€¢ UTILIZE RAPID DATA COLLECTION TOOL/MECHANISM FOR COLLECTION OF SAFETY (ADVERSE EVENTS) AND EFFECTIVENESS (PERFORMANCE) DATA
Â€¢ COLLABORATE WITH BARDA AND BARDA-FUNDED COMPANY SPONSORS OF MEDICAL COUNTERMEASURES ON PATHWAY FOR FDA APPROVAL/LICENSURE UNDER THE ANIMAL RULE TO MEET POST-MARKETING REGULATORY COMMITMENTS
THE BULK OF THIS WORK WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED IN YEAR 1 OF THE BASE PERIOD; MINOR ITERATIONS OF THE WORK ARE REQUIRED ANNUALLY THEREAFTER. COLLABORATORS IN THE USCIITG-PREP NETWORK ARE TASKED WITH COORDINATING REPORTS AND COMPLETING THE WORK REQUIRED AT THEIR RESPECTIVE SITES. DELIVERABLES SPECIFIC FOR THE BASE PERIOD INCLUDE:
1. MONTHLY Â€“ PROGRESS REPORTS TO INCLUDE FINANCIAL INFORMATION AND RESEARCH UPDATES, DUE THE 15TH OF EACH MONTH WITH THE FIRST REPORT DUE ON NOVEMBER 15, 2014
2. YEARLY Â€“ PROGRESS REPORT FOR THE PAST YEARÂ€™S WORK TO INCLUDE BOTH RESEARCH FINDINGS, FINANCIAL UPDATE, AND PUBLICATIONS AND SPEAKING ENGAGEMENTS, DUE NOVEMBER 15TH OF EACH YEAR
3. YEARLY Â€“ OPERATIONS PLAN FOR THE BARDA-SPONSORED PHASE 4 FIELD STUDIES, DUE SEPTEMBER 30TH OF EACH YEAR IF APPLICABLE
4. JANUARY 31, 2015 Â€“ FINAL TREATMENT PROTOCOL FOR TREATING CRITICALLY ILL INFLUENZA PATIENTS WITH IV ZANAMIVIR
5. JULY 30, 2015 Â€“ A COPY OF THE ECRF TO BE USED DURING THE 2015-2016 INFLUENZA SEASON

Sub-Award Description:
I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES
A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT.
THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING.
B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES
STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT.
HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED.
ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION.
II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED
A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.)
ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT.
B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS
LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION.
MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. ADAMS WILL COORDINATE OBTAINING EXISTING MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX ANTIGENS THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH DRS. P. DUFFY, D. KASLOW AND A. HOLDER (SEE LETTERS OF SUPPORT). MURINE PANELS OF MABS WILL BE GENERATED DR. ADAMS (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A MINIMUM OF TEN MURINE ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE OBTAINED THROUGH COLLABORATIONS OR GENERATED.
EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. ADAMS HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA SPOROZOITES OR MEROZOITES. NEUTRALIZATION OF P. FALCIPARUM SPOROZOITES WILL BE EXAMINED BY DR. ADAMS IN ONE OF THREE ASSAYS. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN SPOROZOITE OR MEROZOITE ASSAYS PER YEAR.
MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE AND SPOROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE EVALUATED BY DR. ADAMS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR.
DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. A DATABASE AT WU WILL CATALOG THE DATA GENERATED IN ALL OF THE CONTRACT GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; PROGRESS OF YEAST SURFACE DISPLAY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF MASS SPECTROMETRY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHY EXPERIMENTS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY CORE STRATEGIES; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY ALTERNATE STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. ADAMS WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE.
ALTERNATE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES. IN ADDITION TO THE CORE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES TO BE PERFORMED BY DRS. FREMONT, GROSS AND TOLIA, OUR COLLABORATIVE TEAM HAS EXPERTISE WITH A VARIETY OF COMPLEMENTARY METHODS THAT CAN BE USED AS NEEDED. B CELL EPITOPES MAY BE MAPPED BY PHAGE DISPLAY TECHNOLOGY, A TECHNIQUE SUCCESSFULLY APPLIED BY DR. ADAMS.
C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS
IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE.
HUMAN SUBJECTS INVOLVEMENT, CHARACTERISTICS AND DESIGN
HUMAN: THIS PROJECT WILL OBTAIN HUMAN BLOOD FOR: 1) IMMUNE SERUM ANTIBODIES TO IDENTIFY AND
CHARACTERIZE EPITOPES; 2) PLASMODIUM VIVAX FOR EX VIVO INVASION ASSAYS AND DNA TO ANALYZE
GENETIC DIVERSITY OF DBP; AND 3) UNINFECTED RED BLOOD CELLS (NORMOCYTES, RETICULOCYTES) FOR IN VITRO
BINDING ASSAYS AND EX VIVO INVASION ASSAYS.

ANIMAL: USF COMPARATIVE MEDICINE MAINTAINS AN ANIMAL CARE AND USE PROGRAM IS FULLY
AAALAC ACCREDITED, AS ACCREDITED UNIT #000434. VETERINARIANS AND STAFF PROVIDE
OVERSIGHT OF ANIMAL HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, GUIDANCE AND ASSISTANCE AND EQUIPMENT AND
ROOM SANITATION. ASSOCIATED WITH GHIDR VECTOR BORNE PATHOGEN LAB ARE BSL1 AND BSL2
ANIMAL FACILITIES WITHIN IDRB, COMBINED SPACE WITH PREP ROOM AND AUTOCLAVE IS
APPROXIMATELY 800 SQ. FT., THAT ARE CAPABLE OF SUPPORTING MOST OF LABORATORY ANIMAL
RESEARCH NEEDS OF THE ONGOING PROJECTS.

ALL WORK PERFORMED UNDER THIS CONTRACT WILL BE REPORTED TO THE PROJECT MANAGER AND PROGRAM DIRECTOR AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY ON A QUARTERLY BASIS.
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT.
THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING.

STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT.
HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION.

II.        RECRUITING AND SECURING 3-5 CORE NATIONAL FACULTY TO BE A PART OF THE EXTENDED FACULTY NETWORK TO SERVE AS ADDITIONAL RESOURCES FOR ALL STAKEHOLDERS PARTICIPATING IN AHRQÂ€™S SAFETY PROGRAM FOR AMBULATORY SURGERY.

VI.        PARTICIPATING IN MONTHLY TELECONFERENCE CALLS FOR THE EXTENDED FACULTY NETWORK AND OTHER AD HOC NATIONAL PROGRAM EVENTS (I.E. AHRQ-FUNDED MEETINGS).

III.

Sub-Award Description:
THIS STUDY SHALL PROVIDE A CLINICAL TRIAL COMPARING TWO APPROACHES FOR THE PREVENTION OF CMV I.E., PROPHYLAXIS VERSUS PREEMPTIVE THERAPY IN CMV RECIPIENT NEGATIVE/DONOR POSITIVE (R-/D+) LIVER TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS. THE STUDY ADDRESSES AN IMPORTANT BIOLOGIC CONCEPT, I.E. ALLOWING CONTROLLED ANTIGEN EXPOSURE TO OCCUR AS OPPOSED TO ITS COMPLETE SUPPRESSION MIGHT BETTER FACILITATE PROTECTIVE IMMUNITY NECESSARY FOR LONG-TERM PROTECTION AGAINST CMV. THUS, THE TARGETED APPROACH OF USING PREEMPTIVE THERAPY UPON DETECTION OF VIREMIA MAY INCUR A LOWER RISK OF CMV DISEASE AND LEADS TO GREATER DEVELOPMENT OF CMV-SPECIFIC IMMUNE RESPONSE COMPARED TO PROPHYLAXIS. 
OVER THE LIFE OF THIS SUBCONTRACT AGREEMENT, SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL RECRUIT AND RETAIN APPROXIMATELY THIRTY-SIX (36) CMV R-/D+ LIVER TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS TO COMPLETE THE FINAL PROTOCOL.

Sub-Award Description:
PURPOSE: TO SERVE AS A DESIGNATED OUTREACH LIBRARY FOR THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION OF THE
NATIONAL NETWORK OF LIBRARIES OF MEDICINE.

DESCRIPTION OF WORK: OUTREACH LIBRARIES AGREE TO PERFORM THE FOLLOWING FUNCTIONS ON BEHALF OF THE 
NETWORK:

1.  DESIGNATE A LIBRARIAN TO SERVE AS OUTREACH LIBRARY LIAISON TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION;

2.  PARTICIPATE IN OUTREACH LIBRARY WEBINARS AND OTHER COLLABORATIVE ACTIVITIES PROVIDED FOR 
OUTREACH LIBRARIANS;

3.  ASSIST THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY IN THE IDENTIFICATION OF UNDERSERVED GROUPS OF HEALTH 
PROFESSIONALS AND CONSUMERS WITHIN THE STATE;

4.  PROVIDE UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WITHIN THE STATE WITH REFERENCE SERVICES AND ACCESS 
TO COLLECTIONS, INCLUDING ACCESS TO ELECTRONIC RESOURCES TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY LICENSE 
AGREEMENTS;

5.  PROVIDE DOCUMENT DELIVERY SERVICE TO UNAFFILIATED HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, CONSUMERS AND
NN/LM AFFILIATE MEMBERS IN THE STATE;

6.  PROVIDE TRAINING IN NLM RESOURCES AND DATABASES TO HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, LIBRARIANS AND 
CONSUMERS IN THE STATE. THIS MAY BE DONE AT THE LIBRARY'S OWN INITIATIVE OR IN PARTNERSHIP WITH THE 
REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY;

7.  SUPPORT THE NLM AND NN/LM EXHIBIT PROGRAMS BY ASSISTING IN AND/OR SUPPORTING STAFFING AT STATE 
EXHIBITS COORDINATED BY THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY, BY INFORMING THE REGIONAL MEDICAL LIBRARY 
ABOUT POSSIBLE EXHIBIT OPPORTUNITIES IN THE STATE, AND BY EXHIBITING AT LOCAL COMMUNITY EVENTS;

8.  ENTER NLM AND NN/LM RELATED OUTREACH ACTIVITIES INTO THE APPROPRIATE DATABASE WITHIN 30 DAYS OF 
THE ACTIVITY 

9.  SUBMIT TALLY SHEETS TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION WITHIN 30 DAYS AFTER AN EXHIBIT EVENT 

10. SUBMIT AN ANNUAL REPORT TO THE GREATER MIDWEST REGION, SUMMARIZING OUTREACH ACTIVITIES 
UNDERTAKEN BY THE OUTREACH LIBRARY DURING THE CONTRACT PREVIOUS YEAR 

*NOTE: IN THE FALL, NLM PLANS TO COMBINE THESE THREE REPORTING OPTIONS INTO THE "NLM OUTREACH 
APPLICATION AND ONLINE CONTACT REPORTING SYSTEM" WHICH WILL REPLACE THE OARF DATABASE. ALL OUTREACH 
ACTIVITIES, EXHIBITING EVENTS AND ANNUAL REPORTS WILL BE ENTERED INTO THAT SYSTEM WHEN IT BECOMES 
AVAILABLE.

MEASUREMENT OF PROGREY: PROGRESS WILL BE MEASURED BY MONITORING INPUT FROM THE DESIGNATED OUTREACH 
LIBRARIAN DURING QUARTERLY WEBINARS AND OTHER MEETINGS, LEVEL OF ACTIVITY REPORTED IN THE NLM 
OUTREACH ACTIVITY DATABASE, AND CONTENT OF THE ANNUAL REPORT.

Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

Sub-Award Description:
I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES
A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT.
THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS OF HUMAN WILL BE STUDIED: TWO FLAVIVIRUSES (DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 AND JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS), TWO BUNYAVIRUSES (RIFT VALLEY FEVER AND OROPOUCHE VIRUSES) AND TWO MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). WE HAVE DEVELOPED A STRONG PLAN FOR THE GENERATION OF HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. 
B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES
STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT.
LARGE PANELS OF NEUTRALIZING MABS AGAINST TARGET VIRUSES WILL BE GENERATED BY DR. JAMES CROWE. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR VACCINE TRIALS WILL BE DEVELOPED AGAINST RIFT VALLEY FEVER VIRUS (RVFV), DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 (DENV-4), JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS (JEV) AND OROPOUCHE VIRUS.  
ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION.
II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED
A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.)
ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT.
B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS
LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION.
A CRITICAL ELEMENT OF OUR PROPOSAL IS THE GENERATION OF LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST FLAVIVIRUS AND BUNYAVIRUS TARGETS WILL BE DEVELOPED IN THE CROWE LAB. THE MABS FOR RVFV THAT WILL BE MAPPED IN THIS CONTRACT ARE BEING ISOLATED AS PART OF ONGOING RESEARCH IN COLLABORATION OF TED ROSS, PHD OF VGTI IN FLORIDA. THE DENV-4 HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF SUBJECTS IMMUNIZED WITH A LIVE-ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE THAT HAS BEEN USED SUCCESSFULLY IN HUMAN TRIALS IN COLLABORATION WITH A. DURBIN AND S. WHITEHEAD. THE JEV HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF VOLUNTEERS WHO HAVE RECEIVED A LIVE-ATTENUATED OR INACTIVATED JEV VACCINE IN COLLABORATION WITH S. THOMAS AND FROM CONVALESCENT PBMCS FROM SUBJECTS INFECTED WITH JEV IN THE FIELD IN COLLABORATION WITH C. SIMMONS. FOR THIS CONTRACT, THE CROWE LABORATORY WILL SUPPLY HIGHLY PURIFIED IGG PREPARATIONS OF HUMAN MABS WITH KNOWN FUNCTIONAL ACTIVITY. THE TEXT BELOW DESCRIBES A PLAN FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE MABS.
SOURCE OF HUMAN B CELLS. NATURAL INFECTION. FOR SOME OF THE VIRUSES TARGETED FOR HUMAN MAB PRODUCTION (JEV, RVFV), SOME OF THE SAMPLES WILL BE OBTAINED FROM PERIPHERAL BLOOD CELLS OF OTHERWISE HEALTHY DONORS WHO SUFFERED ACUTE AND CONFIRMED VIRAL INFECTION. THIS WILL BE COORDINATED BY DR. CROWE AND COLLABORATORS (RVFV: DR. MARIETJIE VENTER, UNIVERSITY OF PRETORIA; JEV: DR. CAMERON SIMMONS, OXFORD UNIVERSITY CLINICAL RESEARCH UNIT, VIETNAM). CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM SEVERAL IMMUNE DONORS WILL BE TRANSFERRED IN A COMPLETELY DE-IDENTIFIED FASHION TO THE VANDERBILT VACCINE CENTER IN THE U.S. FOR THESE STUDIES. IMMUNIZATION. PBMCS ARE AVAILABLE FROM A LARGE NUMBER OF VACCINE RECIPIENTS WHO HAVE RECEIVED EITHER THE INACTIVATED RVFV VACCINE OR THE LIVE ATTENUATED MP-12 STRAIN AT USAMRIID IN MARYLAND, A LIVE ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE (NIH AND JOHNS HOPKINS), OR INACTIVATED OR LIVE-ATTENUATED JEV (WRAIR). WITH THE HELP OF OUR COLLABORATORS, SUBJECTS WITH HIGH TITER NEUTRALIZING POLYCLONAL ABS WILL BE IDENTIFIED AND, DR. CROWE WILL OBTAIN DE-IDENTIFIED CELLS FROM VACCINEES. THE USE OF CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM MONOVALENTLY IMMUNIZED INDIVIDUALS IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT FOR DENV-4 AND JEV, AS IN ENDEMIC REGIONS THESE VIRUSES CO-CIRCULATE WITH OTHER FLAVIVIRUSES (E.G., OTHER DENV SEROTYPES AND YELLOW FEVER VIRUS), WHICH CAN SKEW THE ANTIBODY REPERTOIRE TOWARDS MORE CROSS-REACTIVE AND LESS NEUTRALIZING ABS.
MAB TECHNOLOGIES. THE CROWE LAB HAVE SEVERAL B CELL TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL BE USED IN THIS PROJECT. ONE STRATEGY IS TO GENERATE HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS FROM CIRCULATING B CELLS USING AN ELECTROFUSION TECHNIQUE THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND OPTIMIZED. ARGUABLY, THIS APPROACH IS THE HIGHEST EFFICIENCY TECHNIQUE FOR ISOLATING HUMAN CLONES WITH NATURALLY MATCHED HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAIN GENES EVER REPORTED. THE CROWE LAB HAS GENERATED THOUSANDS OF VIRUS-SPECIFIC B CELL LINES AND MABS TO INFLUENZA, DENV, RSV, MPV, HIV, WEST NILE VIRUS AND OTHERS. THE EFFICIENCY OF THIS METHOD ALLOWED FOR GENERATION OF HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS TO THE 1918 H1N1 PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS FROM ~ 100 YEAR OLD SURVIVORS, IN WHOM THE AVERAGE CIRCULATING FREQUENCY OF SPECIFIC B CELLS SPECIFIC WAS 1 IN 4 X 106 CELLS. 
HYBRIDOMA FORMATION. THE CROWE LAB WILL THAW CRYOPRESERVED PBMC AND ISOLATE CELLS USING A FICOLL-HYPAQUE DENSITY GRADIENT METHOD. HUMAN LYMPHOCYTES WILL BE STIMULATED AND TRANSFORMED AFTER INCUBATION WITH EBV SUBSTRAIN B95.8, THE TLR AGONIST CPG ODN 2006 (2.5 ÂΜG/ML; INVIVOGEN), 10 ÂΜM OF CHK2 INHIBITOR II (SIGMA C3742), AND 1 ÂΜG/ML CYCLOSPORIN A. CELLS ARE PLATED IN 384-WELL TISSUE CULTURE PLATES AND MONITORED FOR TRANSFORMATION. TYPICALLY, 50 TO 80 COLONIES FORM PER WELL, WITH ROBUST AB SECRETION.
SCREENING FOR VIRUS-SPECIFIC AB LINES. SUPERNATANTS FROM WELLS CONTAINING EBV-TRANSFORMED LYMPHOBLASTOID CELL LINES (LCL) ARE SCREENED IN THE CROWE LABORATORY FOR VIRUS (RVFV, DENV-4, JEV) NEUTRALIZATION (ATTENUATED STRAINS ONLY) OR BINDING ACTIVITY IN ELISAS AGAINST A PANEL OF VIRAL ANTIGENS (RECOMBINANT SOLUBLE PROTEINS (GC, GN, E PROTEINS), OR INACTIVATED WHOLE VIRUS (RVFV STRAIN MP-12, DENV-4 STRAIN 1036, OR JEV STRAIN 14-14-2). CONCURRENTLY, THE CROWE LAB WILL SEND BY OVERNIGHT EXPRESS SHIPPING AN ALIQUOT OF SUPERNATANT FOR TESTING THE NEXT DAY IN A VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY USING LIVE VIRULENT WILD-TYPE RVFV (AT VGTI IN THE ROSS LABORATORY) DENV-4 (DIAMOND LABORATORY) AND JEV (DIAMOND LABORATORY). POSITIVE WELLS IN ANY OF THE ASSAYS ARE SELECTED FOR EXPANSION AND FUSION.

WE USED A SERIES OF STEMCELL TECHNOLOGIES MEDIA FOR THESE PROCEDURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE CLONACELLÂ®-HY MEDIUM E FOR GROWTH AND EXPANSION. IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE.

HYBRIDOMA FORMATION. THE CROWE LAB WILL THAW CRYOPRESERVED PBMC AND ISOLATE CELLS USING A FICOLL-HYPAQUE DENSITY GRADIENT METHOD. HUMAN LYMPHOCYTES WILL BE STIMULATED AND TRANSFORMED AFTER INCUBATION WITH EBV SUBSTRAIN B95.8, THE TLR AGONIST CPG ODN 2006 (2.5 ÂΜG/ML; INVIVOGEN), 10 ÂΜM OF CHK2 INHIBITOR II (SIGMA C3742), AND 1 ÂΜG/ML CYCLOSPORIN A. CELLS ARE PLATED IN 384-WELL TISSUE CULTURE PLATES AND MONITORED FOR TRANSFORMATION. TYPICALLY, 50 TO 80 COLONIES FORM PER WELL, WITH ROBUST AB SECRETION.
SCREENING FOR VIRUS-SPECIFIC AB LINES. SUPERNATANTS FROM WELLS CONTAINING EBV-TRANSFORMED LYMPHOBLASTOID CELL LINES (LCL) ARE SCREENED IN THE CROWE LABORATORY FOR VIRUS (RVFV, DENV-4, JEV) NEUTRALIZATION (ATTENUATED STRAINS ONLY) OR BINDING ACTIVITY IN ELISAS AGAINST A PANEL OF VIRAL ANTIGENS (RECOMBINANT SOLUBLE PROTEINS (GC, GN, E PROTEINS), OR INACTIVATED WHOLE VIRUS (RVFV STRAIN MP-12, DENV-4 STRAIN 1036, OR JEV STRAIN 14-14-2). CONCURRENTLY, THE CROWE LAB WILL SEND BY OVERNIGHT EXPRESS SHIPPING AN ALIQUOT OF SUPERNATANT FOR TESTING THE NEXT DAY IN A VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY USING LIVE VIRULENT WILD-TYPE RVFV (AT VGTI IN THE ROSS LABORATORY) DENV-4 (DIAMOND LABORATORY) AND JEV (DIAMOND LABORATORY). POSITIVE WELLS IN ANY OF THE ASSAYS ARE SELECTED FOR EXPANSION AND FUSION. 
ELECTROFUSION. EBV-TRANSFORMED LCL SECRETE HUMAN ABS, BUT ARE QUITE UNSTABLE AND DIFFICULT TO CLONE. LCLS SECRETING VIRUS-SPECIFIC MABS ARE FUSED WITH HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS TO FORM HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS, WHICH ARE CONSIDERABLY MORE STABLE. THE SYSTEM USED IS A PROGRAMMABLE ELECTROFUSION SOURCE (CYTOPULSE PA-4000/PA-101). HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS AND EBV-TRANSFORMED HUMAN B CELLS ARE WASHED WITH RPMI-1640 AND CYTOFUSION MEDIUM. LARGE VOLUME FUSION CHAMBERS ARE COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE AND INTERFACE WELL WITH THIS UNIT. THE KEY TO THE FUSION IS BRINGING THE TWO CELL TYPES INTO CLOSE PHYSICAL CONTACT. AFTER FUSION, CELLS ARE ALLOWED TO RECOVER IN THE FUSION ELECTRODE FOR 30 MINUTES, HARVESTED, AND THEN WASHED ONCE WITH RPMI-1640 AT ROOM TEMPERATURE PRIOR TO PLATING IN SELECTION PLATES. 
HYBRIDOMA SELECTION AND CLONING. FUSED CELLS ARE SEEDED INTO 384-WELL PLATES IN COMPLETE MEDIUM CONTAINING HAT AND OUABAIN. AFTER FIVE DAYS OF CULTURE, CELLS ARE FED WITH FRESH MEDIUM CONTAINING HYPOXANTHINE/THYMIDINE OR HT. WE USED A SERIES OF STEMCELL TECHNOLOGIES MEDIA FOR THESE PROCEDURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE CLONACELLÂ®-HY MEDIUM E FOR GROWTH AND EXPANSION. AFTER INITIAL SCREENING FOR HUMAN AB PRODUCTION BY ELISA, THE HYBRIDOMA CELLS FROM POSITIVE WELLS ARE EXPANDED INTO 96- AND THEN 24-WELL PLATES AND CULTURED IN COMPLETE MEDIUM AND THEN HYBRIDOMA CELLS ARE SEEDED IN 96-WELL PLATES AT 0.3 CELL-PER-WELL DENSITY. LIMITING DILUTION IS PERFORMED TWICE TO ENSURE THAT HYBRIDOMA CLONES ARE GENERATED. ALTERNATIVELY, WE CAN SINGLE-CELL SORT THE LINES ON A FACSARIA III FLOW OR USE A CLONEPIX INSTRUMENT. CULTURE SUPERNATANTS ARE SCREENED BY ELISA FOR HUMAN IGG AND ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC ABS. THE COATING ANTIGENS INCLUDE INACTIVATED VIRUSES, LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS PARTICLES, AND RECOMBINANT ENVELOPE GLYCOPROTEINS. 
MAB PREPARATIONS. HYBRIDOMA CELL LINES WILL BE ADAPTED TO SERUM-FREE MEDIUM. SUPERNATANTS OF HIGH-DENSITY CULTURES WILL BE PRODUCED IN CELLINE DEVICES (BD BIOSCIENCES). PURIFIED AND CONCENTRATED PREPARATIONS OF EACH MAB WILL BE PREPARED BY FPLC USING PROTEIN G RESIN ON AN AKTA INSTRUMENT FOLLOWED BY BUFFER EXCHANGE USING ULTRA CENTRIFUGAL FILTER DEVICES. FOR LARGER SCALE PREPARATIONS (E.G., 50 TO 100 MG LOTS), WE WILL SCALE THE CELL CULTURE UP TO 25 L USING A WAVE BIOREACTOR. VOLUME WILL BE INITIALLY REDUCED USING A GE QUIXSTAND LABORATORY-SCALE SEPARATION SYSTEM THAT USES CROSS-FLOW FILTRATION CARTRIDGES. THIS PROCEDURE IS FOLLOWED BY FPLC PURIFICATION. WE WILL USE QUANTITATIVE ELISAS TO DEFINE THE FINAL CONCENTRATION OF MABS. 

C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS
IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE.
HUMANS: DR. CROWE WILL BE CREATING HUMAN MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES. THERE WILL BE NO IDENTIFIERS LINKED TO THE DATA BEING TRANSFERRED TO WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY.

IF SUCH CHANGES ARE REQUESTED BEYOND THIS TIME FRAME, SUBMISSION OF A NEW PROPOSAL IS REQUIRED.

Sub-Award Description:
THE OVERARCHING LONG-TERM GOAL OF THE
PROJECT IS TO CHARACTERIZE IMMUNE
MARKERS AND MECHANISMS IN THE ELDERLY
THAT DETERMINE THEIR VULNERABILITY TO
INFECTIONS AND BIOTERRORISM AGENTS,
SPECIFICALLY WEST NILE VIRUS (WNV).
ELDERLY HUMANS ARE HIGHLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO
WNV COMPARED TO IMMUNOCOMPETENT
ADULTS, AND WNV READILY INFECTS MICE,
WHERE THE DISEASE IS HIGHLY LETHAL TO OLD ANIMALS AND RECAPITULATES MANY
ESSENTIAL FEATURES OF THE HUMAN DISEASE.
PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR AT OREGON HEALTH
AND SCIENCE UNIVERSITY (OHSU) WILL
OVERSEE WNV MICRORNA EXPERIMENTS
AND THE WORK COMPLETED BY THE
CO-PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS, POSTDOCTORAL
RESEARCHER, SENIOR RESEARCH ASSISTANT,
AND RESEARCH ASSISTANT 2. OHSU WILL
IDENTIFY MICRO RNAS WITHIN SPECIFIED CELL TYPES FROM ADULT AND OLD ORGANISMS
USING MASSIVELY (“DEEP”)
SEQUENCING-BASED TECHNIQUES. THESE METHODS ARE EXPECTED TO PROVIDE BOTH SEQUENCE AND QUALITY INFORMATION FOR EACH MIRNA, REGARDLESS OF WHETHER THE MIRNA HAS BEEN PREVIOUSLY IDENTIFIED.
SPECIFICALLY, THE CO-PRINCIPAL
INVESTIGATORS WILL ANALYZE MIRNA
EXPRESSION IN DCS AND T-CELLS FROM AND
ADULT MICE AND HUMANS, WORK WITH THE
UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA LAB TO DETERMINE
THE CONTRIBUTION OF THESE MIRNAS TO 
FUNCTIONAL DEFECTS OBSERVED IN THESE
CELLS AND WORK WITH POSTDOCTORAL
RESEARCHER TO DETERMINE MRNA
TARGEST OF AGE-MISREGULATED MIRNAS AND
THUS HELP PROVIDE A MECHANISTIC BASIS
FOR AGE-RELATED MULTIFUNCTION OF CELLS OF THE IMMUNE SYSTEM AND PROVIDE
STATISTICAL OVERSIGHT AND ASSIST WITH
EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN AND OVERSEE
ACTIVITIES OF SENIOR RESEARCH
ASSISTANT AND RESEARCH ASSISTANT. THE
POSTDOCTORAL RESEARCHER WILL IDENTIFY
TARGETS AFFECTED BY AGE-MISREGULATED
MIRNAS AND DETERMINE THE ROLES THESE
TARGETS PLAY IN AGE-RELATED DEFECTS IN
IMMUNITY. THE SENIOR RESEARCH
ASSISTANT WILL LEAD THE MIRNA AND
PATHWAY ANALYSIS. THE RESEARCH
ASSISTANT 2 WILL OVERSEE ALL DATA DISSEMINATION FOLLOWING THE DATA SHARING PLAN. ADDITIONALLY, OHSU WILL PARTICIPATE IN MEETINGS WITH UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA AS PROJECT PROGRESSES, INCLUDING TRAVELING TO UNIVERSITY OF ARIZONA.

Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

PSC.description: HEALTH R&D SERVICES; HEALTH CARE SERVICES; APPLIED RESEARCH

Sub-Award Description:
I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES
A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT.
THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING.
B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES
STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT.
HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED.
ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION.
II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED
A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.)
ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT.
 
B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS
LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION.
MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. KING WILL GENERATE HUMAN ANTI-MALARIA MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE GENERATED.
EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. KING HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA MEROZOITES. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN PER YEAR.
MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE CARRIED OUT BY DR. KING. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR.
DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. A DATABASE AT WU WILL CATALOG THE DATA GENERATED IN ALL OF THE CONTRACT GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; PROGRESS OF YEAST SURFACE DISPLAY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF MASS SPECTROMETRY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHY EXPERIMENTS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY CORE STRATEGIES; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY ALTERNATE STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. KING WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE.
C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS
IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE.
HUMANS: AS INDICATED IN HIS PROTECTION OF HUMAN SUBJECTS/ASSURANCE IDENTIFICATION/IRB CERTIFICATION/DECLARATION OF EXEMPTION, DR. CHRISTOPHER KINGÂ€™S CURRENT PROPOSAL UTILIZES HUMAN SUBJECT MATTER THAT IS DE-IDENTIFIED AND DOES NOT QUALIFY AS HUMAN SUBJECTS RESEARCH ACCORDING TO FEDERAL REGULATIONS.  ANY POTENTIAL CHANGES IN THE SCOPE OF WORK THAT WOULD REQUIRE HUMAN SUBJECTS MATERIAL WILL BE DISCUSSED AND APPROVED BY APPROPRIATE INSTITUTIONAL AND NIH OFFICIALS PRIOR TO THE START OF WORK.
ANIMALS: NONE

ALL WORK PERFORMED UNDER THIS CONTRACT WILL BE REPORTED TO THE PROJECT MANAGER AND PROGRAM DIRECTOR AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY ON A QUARTERLY BASIS.
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

OPTION 11B - 400 ANIMAL SURVEILLANCE SAMPLES (0258-0572-4609)

FERRETS (MUSTELA PUTORIUS FURO) ARE NATURALLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO HUMAN INFLUENZA VIRUSES A AND THEIR DISEASE RESPONSE TO INFECTION WIDELY RESEMBLES THAT OF HUMANS INCLUDING CLINICAL SIGNS, PATHOGENESIS AND IMMUNITY (1-6).  FERRETS ARE ALSO SUSCEPTIBLE TO AVIAN, EQUINE AND SWINE INFLUENZA A VIRUSES, ALTHOUGH ONLY SWINE AND HUMAN A VIRUSES INDUCE FEBRILE ILLNESSES IN FERRETS (7, 8). THE FERRET ALSO DISPLAYS PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS THAT ALLOW EASY IDENTIFICATION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF CLINICAL SYMPTOMS.  THE UNUSUALLY LONG TRACHEA ALLOWS EASY COMPARTMENTALIZATION OF THE UPPER AND LOWER RESPIRATORY TRACTS (9, 10).  THE FERRET IS LARGE ENOUGH TO MONITOR CLINICAL PARAMETERS SUCH AS TEMPERATURE, PULSE AND RESPIRATORY RATE WHILE ALSO BEING THE ONLY SMALL ANIMAL TO DEVELOPS A FEBRILE RESPONSE TO NATURALLY OCCURRING INFLUENZA A VIRUSES (10). 

ANTIGENIC CHARACTERIZATION OF INFLUENZA VIRUSES IS TYPICALLY BASED ON HEMAGGLUTINATION INHIBITION (HI) ASSAY DATA FOR VIRAL ISOLATES TESTED AGAINST STRAIN-SPECIFIC POST-INFECTION FERRET ANTISERA. THE GOAL OF THIS SUBCONTRACT IS TO PREPARE FERRET SERA AGAINST HUMAN INFLUENZA VIRUSES. FERRETS WILL BE INOCULATED WITH A HIGH DOSE (≥106 TCID50) OF HUMAN INFLUENZA VIRUS IN 1 ML INOCULUM (TABLE 1). TWO FERRETS/VIRUS WILL BE USED. FERRETS WILL BE MONITORED FOR CLINICAL SIGNS OF DISEASE. AT 14 DAYS-POST-INOCULATION (DPI), 2-3 ML OF BLOOD ARE COLLECTED TO TEST HI TITER AGAINST HOMOLOGOUS VIRUS, IF THE ANTIBODY TITER HAS REACHED ≥ 640, THEN COLLECT FULL BLOOD. SACRIFICE. IF THE ANTIBODY TITER HAS NOT YET REACHED THE EXPECTED TITER, PERFORM ADDITIONAL IMMUNIZATION, FOOTPAD SQ INJECTION OF 0.4 ML (INACTIVATED VIRUS+ADJUVANT)*/FOOTPAD. AT 14 DAYS-POST-BOOST, BLEED OUT AND TEST HI TITERS AGAINST HOMOLOGOUS VIRUS.

Sub-Award Description:
DRS. MARK GLADWIN AND TAMIR KANIAS WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE STUDY DESIGN, PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT, HUMAN SUBJECT RESEARCH COMPLIANCE, PERFORM RATE OF HEMOLYSIS ASSAYS AND DATA ANALYSIS, SHIP REPOSITORY SAMPLES TO BLOOD SYSTEMS RESEARCH INSTITUTE (BSRI) AND REPORT RESULTS TO BSRI AND RESEARCH TRIANGLE INTERNATIONAL (RTI).

TRAINING/MOP
DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL PROVIDE TRAINING TO BSRI STAFF IN PERFORMING THE SELECTED HIGH-THROUGHPUT ASSAYS MEASURING UP TO 4 FORMS OF STRESS:  OXIDANT-INDUCED STRESS, SHEAR OR MECHANICAL STRESS, OSMOTIC STRESS AND STORAGE HEMOLYSIS. DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL SHARE ALL PROTOCOLS RELATED TO ASSAYS AND INFORMATION REQUIRED TO SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE MANUAL OF PROCEDURES FOR THE STUDY WITH BSRI IN COLLABORATION WITH RTI, THE REDS-III DATA COORDINATING CENTER.

PILOT/QC
DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL PARTICIPATE IN A PILOT STUDY WITH BSRI TO COMPARE HEMOLYSIS PARAMETERS DURING STORAGE IN THE MANUFACTURED LEUKO-REDUCED PACKED RED BLOOD CELLS AND TRANSFER BAGS FROM EACH OF THE 4 HUBS, AND COMPARE THE REPRODUCIBILITY OF THE ASSAYS ACROSS THE TWO TESTING LABS (UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH (UP) AND BSRI).

SCREENING FOR EXTREME HEMOLYSIS PHENOTYPES
A TOTAL OF 14,000 RBC DONORS WILL BE ENROLLED ACROSS FOUR REDS-III HUBS IN A MULTI-CENTER STUDY TO IDENTIFY NOVEL POLYMORPHISMS IN HEMOGLOBIN AND IRON REGULATORY PROTEINS, TO DEFINE THE GENETIC AND METABOLIC BASES FOR DONOR SPECIFIC DIFFERENCES IN STORAGE HEMOLYSIS AND TO ESTABLISH A SHARABLE REPOSITORY OF RED BLOOD CELLS (RBC), PLASMA, WHITE BLOOD CELLS, AND DNA SAMPLES FROM DONORS WHO WERE CHARACTERIZED FOR HEMOGLOBIN PARAMETERS, IRON METABOLISM, RBC STORAGE HEMOLYSIS PROPENSITY, AND GENETIC AND METABOLOMIC PROFILES.  DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB AT UP WILL RECEIVE LEUKOCYTE REDUCED-PACKED RED BLOOD CELL (LR-PRBC) SAMPLES IN SMALLER VOLUME BLOOD BAGS FROM THREE (3) OF THE REDS-III BLOOD CENTERS (APPROX.10,500 DONORS).   DURING THE INITIAL SCREENING, THE BAGS WILL BE ACCESSED USING STERILE TECHNIQUES TO ACQUIRE SAMPLES CORRESPONDING TO LR-RBC COMPONENTS STORED FOR 42 DAYS OF STORAGE.   SAMPLES (~120/WEEK) FROM EACH BAG AT THE 40-42 DAY STORAGE TIME POINT WILL BE TESTED WITH SELECTED HIGH-THROUGHPUT ASSAYS (SPONTANEOUS HEMOLYSIS AND OSMOTIC STRESS). THIS COHORT OF REDS-III DONORS WITH LINKED RBC DONATION-DERIVED SAMPLES WILL ENABLE ANALYSIS OF KEY RBC STORAGE PARAMETERS AS A FUNCTION OF DONOR CHARACTERISTICS INCLUDING DEMOGRAPHICS, SMOKING HISTORY, AND FIRST-TIME/REPEAT AND ABO BLOOD GROUP STATUS. THE DATA WILL BE ANALYZED AND REPORTED TO IDENTIFY 1000 DONORS WITH EXTREME RATES OF HEMOLYSIS PHENOTYPES TO BE RECALLED IN THE SECOND PHASE OF THE STUDY.  IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT 800 WILL BE ENROLLED IN THE RECALL STUDY AND WILL PROVIDE DONATION OF ONE FULL LR-PRBC UNIT ALLOWING FOR AMPLE VOLUME TO TEST 3 OR MORE STORAGE TIME POINTS USING EXPANDED TESTING MEASURING UP TO 4 FORMS OF STRESS:  OXIDANT-INDUCED STRESS, SHEAR OR MECHANICAL STRESS, OSMOTIC STRESS AND STORAGE HEMOLYSIS.  UP WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE FOLLOW UP TESTING ON Â¾ (600) OF THE RECALLED DONORS.

BIOSPECIMEN REPOSITORY/BIOLINCC DOCUMENTATION DR. GLADWINÂ€™S LAB WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE STORAGE (-86 DEGREE CELSIUS MECHANICAL FREEZER PROVIDED BY BSRI) OF MULTIPLE ALIQUOTS OF CONCENTRATED RED-BLOOD CELLS AND SUPERNATANT FLUID (ADDITIVE SOLUTION AND LEFT OVER PLASMA) AT EACH TIME POINT TESTED, DURING BOTH THE INITIAL SCREENING AND RECALL STUDY.  THE LAB WILL USE VALIDATED SPECIMEN ACQUISITION AND STORAGE SOPS, AND WILL HAVE AN ACTIVE QA/QC PROGRAM TO ENSURE THAT THE SOPS ARE BEING FOLLOWED.

SHIPMENT
VMI WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR SHIPMENT OF SPECIFIC ALIQUOTS TO DR. ZIMRINGÂ€™S LAB AT PUGET SOUND BLOOD CENTER (PSBC) FOR FURTHER METABOLOMIC TESTING AND QUARTERLY SHIPMENT OF FINAL REPOSITORY ALIQUOTS TO BSRI.

INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL PROGRAMS.

D.   TRAVEL TO AN AREA LIBRARY/ARCHIVES FOR ADVISE AND EXPERTISE
4.   STRIVE TO INCREASE COMMUNITY PATRONAGE OF LIBRARY SERVICES.
A.  TWO (2) STUDENT INTERNS WILL BE SELECTED TO WORK TWENTY HOURS WEEKLY IN THE
CCCC LIBRARY. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES ARE TO ASSIST LIBRARY STAFF TO PREPARE HEALTH ACQUISITIONS 
FOR THE SHELVES, PROVIDE ASSISTANCE AND EDUCATION TO LIBRARY PATRONS, AND MAINTAIN EVENING HOURS TO 
INCREASE LIBRARY PATRONAGE. EMPHASIS WILL BE ON PROMOTION OFLIBRARIANSHIP AS A CAREER DUE TO 
LIMITED AVAILABILITY OF LIBRARIANS IN RURAL, ISOLATED AREAS. LIBRARY INTERNS MAY PARTICIPATE IN 
LIBRARY STAFF TRAINING.
B.  PARTNERSHIP WITH TECHNOLOGY AND MEDIA DEPARTMENTS WILL BE FORMED TO RECORD PUBLIC SERVICE 
ANNOUNCEMENTS AND DESIGN POSTERS UTILIZING LIBRARY INTERNS, COMMUNITY YOUTH, AND COLLEGE STUDENTS.
C.  CONTINUED GROWTH OF HEALTH ACQUISITIONS TO INCREASE HOLDINGS ON HEALTH TOPICS FOR THEVMML.
D.  PROVIDE A MONTHLY PARENT'S NIGHT AND CHILDREN'S NIGHT TO EDUCATE DAKOTA CULTURE, VALUES, COMMON 
HEALTH RISKS/PREVENTION, AND ACTIVITIES.

NARRATIVE:

OBJECTIVE 1 ADDRESSES THE HEALTH DISPARITIES WITHIN THE SPIRIT LAKE TRIBAL COMMUNITY. THE SPIRIT 
LAKE TRIBE HAS A HISTORY OF SOCIAL, HEALTH, ECONOMIC AND EDUCATIONAL HARDSHIP SIMILAR TO OTHER 
TRIBES IN THE NORTHERN PLAINS. ACCORDING TO THE BUREAU OFLNDIAN AFFAIRS (BIA) LABOR FORCE REPORT 
(20014), THE TOTAL POPULATION FOR SPRIT LAKE WAS 7,108 WITH 5002 ENROLLED MEMBERS. APPROXIMATELY 
2921 OFTHOSE ENROLLED ARE OVER THE AGE OF 15 AND UNDER 64 FOLLOWED BY 1865 MEMBERS BEING UNDER16. 
FINALLY 190 MEMBERS ARE AGES 65 AND OVER.

THE POVERTY RATE ON THE RESERVATION IS 51% WITH A MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME OF$15,395 (CENSUS
2000). THE UNEMPLOYMENT RATE ON THE RESERVATION IS 57% (BIA LABOR FORCE REPORT 2005) WITH
THE COMMUNITY'S GRADUATION RATE BEING 51% (ND DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC INSTRUCTION, 2012).

IT IS DESIGNED TO FURTHER ELUCIDATE AND CLARIFY THE LONG-TERM EFFECT OF THE ACCORTD TREATMENT STRATEGIES AND PROVIDE ADDITIONAL DATA ON THE LONG-TERM RELATIONSHIPS AMONG VARIOUS CARDIOVASCULAR AND DIABETIC RISK FACTORS.  ACCORD WAS A RANDOMIZED CARDIOVASCULAR CLINICAL TRIAL IN PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES WHO WERE TREATED AND FOLLOWED FOR AN AVERAGE OF APPROXIMATELY 5 YEARS FROM 2001 THROUGH MID-2009.  ACCORD PARTICIPANTS WHO AGREE TO PARTICIPATE IN THE FOLLOW-ON STUDY WILL CONTINUE TO BE FOLLOWED THROUGH CLINIC AND PHONE VISITS FOR AN AVERAGE OF 3.5 YEARS IN THE PERIOD 2011 THROUGH 2014.  PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA.  THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT.  SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME.  LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

Sub-Award Description: THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO 1) APPLY HIGH THROUGHPUT GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES ON THE WELL-CHARACTERIZED WOMEN'S HEALTH INITIATIVE BIO RESOURCE AND TO 2) INTEGRATE THE DATA GENERATED WITH EXISTING CLINICAL, GENETIC, AND BIOMARKER DATA IN ORDER TO CONFIDENTLY IDENTIFY NOVEL DETERMINANTS OF CORONARY HEART DISEASE AND RELATED PHENOTYPES IN AGING POST-MENOPAUSAL WOMEN" WE PROPOSE TO CAREFULLY PROFILE THE DNA AND PLASMA OF CHD CASES AS WELL AS AN APPROPRIATE SET OF CONTROLS USING TWO COMPLEMENTARY BUT WELL-VALIDATED GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES AT BASELINE .. THESE GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES ARE EXPECTED TO GENERATE HIGH QUALITY AND HIGH-RESOLUTION GENOME WIDE DNA METHYLATION PROFILE AS WELL AS A COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT OF CIRCULATING MICRORNA LEVELS. WE WILL THEN COMPREHENSIVELY ANALYZE AND INTEGRATE THIS GENOMIC DATA WITH EXISTING CLINICAL, GENETIC, AND BIOMARKER DATA USING STATE OF THE ART STATISTICAL METHODOLOGIES DEVELOPED BY MEMBERS OF THE INVESTIGATIVE TEAM TO IDENTIFY GENOMIC SIGNATURES AND PATHWAYS RELEVANT TO CHD AND ITS RISK FACTORS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL ALLOW US AND OTHERS 1) TO IDENTIFY GENOMIC BIOMARKERS OF CHD EVENTS, 2) TO INTEGRATE THESE BIOMARKERS INTO DIAGNOSTIC AND PROGNOSTIC PREDICTORS OF CHD AND RELATED PHENOTYPES, 3) TO ELUCIDATE THE BIOLOGY OF CHD AND RELATED PHENOTYPES, 4) TO TEST WHETHER AGING RELATED CPGS FOUND IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES MEDIATE THE RISK OF AGE ON CHD, AND 5) TO REVISIT THE GWAS STUDIES OF CHD BASED ON MOLECULARLY REFINED PHENOTYPES AND SNP SET ANALYSIS INFORMED BY OUR NEW GENOMIC DATA. THESE OBJECTIVES ARE ACHIEVABLE IN THE CONTEXT OF OUR PRIOR EXPERIENCE PRODUCING AND ANALYZING SIMILAR DATA IN OTHER SAMPLES SETS AS EXTENSIVELY DESCRIBED IN THE "TECHNICAL PLAN" SECTION OF THIS PROPOSAL. THESE OBJECTIVES ARE ALSO ACHIEVABLE IN THE CONTEXT OF THE NUMEROUS UNIQUE STATISTICAL TOOLS WE HAVE DEVELOPED SPECIFICALLY FOR INTEGRATING GENOMIC DATA GENERATED FROM VARIOUS SOURCES.

PARTICIPANTS WILL BE SEEN IN 76 CLINICS ACROSS THE UNITED STATES AND CANADA.  THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A MAJOR CARDIOVASCULAR EVENT.  SECONDARY OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE ALL CAUSE MORTALITY, OTHER MACRO VASCULAR SECONDARY OUTCOMES, AND DISEASE-FREE SURVIVAL TIME.  LAB AND ECG MEASUREMENTS WILL ALSO BE TAKEN PERIODICALLY DURING THE STUDY.

Sub-Award Description:
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL UNDERTAKE THE FOLLOWING TASKS IN COMPLETING THIS WORK:  

  

PROVIDE OVERALL LEADERSHIP AND ADMINISTRATIVE OVERSIGHT FOR THE PROPOSED PROJECT, INVOLVING CO-INVESTIGATORS RABIN AND DAVIES. 

PROVIDE EXPERT INPUT ON A LITERATURE REVIEW AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCAN AIMED AT DEVELOPING AN INVENTORY OF EXISTING CPMS FOR BOTH USE-CASES, AS WELL AS A SET OF PRELIMINARY CRITERIA FOR JUDGING THE QUALITY AND CLINICAL APPLICABILITY OF CPMS.  THIS WORK WILL BE LED BY DR. RABIN, BUILDING ON PRIOR WORK BY HER TEAM AND OTHERS (EPROGNOSIS.ORG RESEARCH GROUP, CPM DEVELOPERS) TO PRODUCE CLINICAL TOOLS AIMED AT MAKING CPMS ACCESSIBLE TO CLINICIANS AND PATIENTS.  THE CONTRACTOR WILL FOCUS ON CPMS FOR PROSTATE CANCER AND HEAD AND NECK CANCER TREATMENT OUTCOMES.  OTHER CANDIDATE CPMS FOR BOTH USE CASES WILL BE IDENTIFIED THROUGH FURTHER LITERATURE REVIEW. 

LEAD DEVELOPMENT OF A PROTOTYPE MODEL OF USE FOR INCORPORATING CPMS RELEVANT TO TREATMENT DECISIONS FOR PROSTATE CANCER, AND REFINE THIS MODEL BASED ON ITERATIVE FEEDBACK OF EXPERT ADVISORY PANEL (EAP) MEMBERS, CONSISTING OF PRACTICING CLINICIANS (UROLOGISTS, MEDICAL ONCOLOGISTS), CANCER SURVIVORS WITH FOCUSED CONTENT EXPERTISE AND EXPERIENCE IN PROSTATE CANCER, AND CPM DEVELOPERS.  THE MODEL OF USE WILL 1) IDENTIFY EXISTING CPMS OF SUFFICIENT QUALITY AND RELEVANCE TO THE TREATMENT DECISION, 2) CLARIFY THE VALUE AND LIMITATIONS OF EACH CPM, AND 3) SPECIFY THE APPROPRIATE MANNER AND SEQUENCE OF USE OF EACH CPM IN THE PATIENT COUNSELING AND DECISION-MAKING PROCESS.  THE TEAMS WILL USE LOGIC MODELS AND STORYBOARDING TO DEPICT THE INFORMATION NEEDS OF CLINICIANS AND PATIENTS WHO ARE ENGAGING IN DECISION MAKING, AND TO REFINE THE PROTOTYPE MODELS OF USE.   

PROVIDE EXPERT INPUT ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF A PROTOTYPE WEB-BASED CLINICAL META-TOOL THAT OPERATIONALIZES THE USE OF PROGNOSTIC MODELS IN CANCER CARE DECISIONS.  THE META-TOOL PROTOTYPE WILL UTILIZE INTERACTIVITY AND INNOVATIVE VISUALIZATION TECHNIQUES TO ENHANCE THE UNDERSTANDABILITY AND USABILITY OF INFORMATION, AS WELL AS LANGUAGE SCRIPTS FOR EXPLAINING THE VALUE AND LIMITATIONS OF PROGNOSTIC ESTIMATES.  THE TOOL WILL INCORPORATE EXPLANATORY LANGUAGE AND SCRIPTS DEVELOPED WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF EAP MEMBERS.  

 

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL NOT BE INVOLVED IN WRITING ANY SPECIFIC FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES THAT MIGHT DEVELOP FROM THIS WORK.  HOWEVER, THE OUTPUT OF THIS CONTRACT IS EXPECTED TO INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF POTENTIAL FUNDING OPPORTUNITIES IN THIS AREA, AND WILL BE USED.  FOR EXAMPLE, PRESENTATIONS TO SENIOR NCI LEADERSHIP AND TO OTHER INTERESTED RESEARCHERS, TO CONTINUE THE DEVELOPMENT OF THIS AREA AS A RESEARCH PROGRAM FOR NCI.

Sub-Award Description:
THE GOALS OF THE ATR PROGRAM CENTER ON THE PROVISION OF SUBSTANCE ABUSE CLINICAL AND RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES TO THOSE IN NEED. THIS GRANT PROGRAM IS DESIGNED TO BE A SYSTEMS- CHANGE INITIATIVE THROUGH THE INTRODUCTION OF A VOUCHER-BASED SYSTEM OF PAYMENT INTO THE CLINICAL TREATMENT DELIVERY SYSTEM, ENCOURAGING INDIVIDUAL CHOICE BY EMPOWERING THE INDIVIDUAL TO CHOOSE HIS/HER PROVIDER OF SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS CLINICAL TREATMENT AND/OR RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES. THROUGH THIS CONTRACT, TA WILL BE PROVIDED TO STATE/T~IBES TO IMPLEMENT A LARGE-SCALE VOUCHERS SYSTEM THAT SUPPORTS THE CONTINUUM OF RECOVERY FROM SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS. ADDITIONALLY, THIS CONTRACT WILL SUPPORT PEER PROVIDERS WHO RECEIVE FEDERAL FUNDING TO BOTH PROVIDE PEER RECOVERY SUPPORT SERVICES THROUGH RECOVERY CENTERS, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, ETC. AND INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT AND CAPACITY-BUILDING FOR THE
DEVELOPMENT OF A STATEWIDE NETWORK OF RECOVERY COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS THAT SERVE TO PROMOTE THE INVOLVEMENT
OF INDIVIDUALS IN RECOVERY FROM ADDICTION, AND THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS AS PARTNERS IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND OTHER ALLIED HEALTH SYSTEMS.

SUBCONTRACTOR HAS BEEN HIRED TO ASSIST THE GRANTEES WITH UNDERSTANDING AND IMPLEMENTING EMPOWERMENT EVALUATION INTO THEIR ATR PROGRAMS.  THE TASKS ARE DESIGNED TO ENCOURAGE THE GRANTEES TO IDENTIFY THE IMPORTANCE OF EVALUATION FOR THEIR PROGRAMS AND HOW BY INCLUDING THEIR COALITIONS AND CLIENTS IN THE PROCESS, THE ATR PROJECT CAN BE ENHANCED.  SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE MOTIVATING THE ATR GRANTEES TO SEE HOW EVALUATION CAN ASSIST THEM WITH SUSTAINING THEIR PROJECTS.  

TASK 1:  SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP CONTENT FOR A TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE (TA) PACKAGE FOR GRANTEES ON HOW TO UTILIZE EMPOWERMENT EVALUATION WITHIN THEIR ATR PROGRAMS AND/OR WITH THEIR PROVIDERS IN THEIR ATR PROGRAMS.

TASK 2: SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DEVELOP CONTENT AND PRESENT THREE MINI WEBINARS/Â€?COFFEE BREAKSÂ€?.  THE FIRST WEBINAR TITLED, Â€ŒEMPOWERMENT EVALUATION: A TOOL FOR PROGRAM IMPROVEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITYÂ€? IS TAKING PLACE AUGUST 13, 2015.  THE PURPOSE OF THIS WEBINAR IS TO HIGHLIGHT THE PURPOSE OF EMPOWERMENT EVALUATION, AS WELL AS THE PRINCIPLES AND CONCEPTS GUIDING THE APPROACH.  IN ADDITION, SPECIFIC STEPS USED TO FACILITATE THE PROCESS WILL BE DISCUSSED.  IMPLICATIONS FOR PROGRAM IMPROVEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY WILL ALSO BE HIGHLIGHTED.

TASK 3:  SUBCONTRACTOR WILL INITIATE PLANNING FOR TWO TAÂ€™S FOR WASHINGTON ATR PROGRAM.

Awarding Sub Agency: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration

ALL PUBLICATIONS AND COMMUNICATIONS RESULTING FROM THIS AGREEMENT SHALL COMPLY WITH THE AHRQ PUBLICATIONS AND COMMUNICATIONS GUIDELINES. THE AHRQ PUBLISHING AND COMMUNICATION STYLE GUIDELINES CAN BE FOUND AT HTTP://WWW.AHRQ.GOV/NEWS/PUBCOMGUIDE/. ANY DELIVERABLES THAT DOES NOT COMPLY WITH THE AHRQ PUBLISHING AND COMMUNICATION STYLE GUIDELINES WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED AS NON-COMPLIANT. 

MANUSCRIPT REVIEW
THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL SUBMIT THE DRAFTS OF ALL MANUSCRIPTS FROM THIS PROJECT TO THE CONTRACTOR FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL BEFORE SUBMISSION FOR PUBLICATION. THE MANUSCRIPTS SHOULD CLEARLY STATE THE LIMITATIONS ON THE GENERALIZABILITY OF THE FINDINGS RESULTING FROM THE RESEARCH METHODOLOGY AND THE STATE OF THE AVAILABLE LITERATURE. MANUSCRIPTS SHALL BE PREPARED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE AHRQ PUBLISHING AND COMMUNICATIONS GUIDELINES STATED ABOVE.
  
BACKGROUND: HEALTHCARE-ASSOCIATED INFECTIONS, OR HAIS, ARE A HIGHLY SIGNIFICANT CAUSE OF ILLNESS AND DEATH FOR PATIENTS IN THE U.S. HEALTH CARE SYSTEM. AT ANY GIVEN TIME, HAIS AFFECT ONE OUT OF EVERY 25 HOSPITAL INPATIENTS. MORE THAN A MILLION OF THESE INFECTIONS OCCUR ACROSS OUR HEALTH CARE SYSTEM EVERY YEAR, LEADING TO SIGNIFICANT PATIENT HARM AND THE ANNUAL LOSS OF TENS OF THOUSANDS OF LIVES, AND COSTING BILLIONS OF DOLLARS EACH YEAR. SOME OF THE MOST PREVALENT HAIS INCLUDE: SURGICAL SITE INFECTIONS (SSIS), CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (CAUTI), CENTRAL-LINE ASSOCIATED BLOOD STREAM INFECTIONS (CLABSI), AND VENTILATOR-ASSOCIATED PNEUMONIA (VAP). IT IS ESTIMATED THAT CAUTIS AFFECT APPROXIMATELY 400,000 HOSPITAL PATIENTS PER YEAR, AND APPROXIMATELY 40,000 CLABSI CASES OCCUR ANNUALLY WITH A MORTALITY RATE FROM 12 TO 25 PERCENT.

Sub-Awardee Name: UNIVERSITY OF VERMONT & STATE AGRICULTURAL COLLEGE
Sub-Award Description:
INDEPENDENTLY AND NOT AS AN AGENT OF THE CONTRACT BREAST CANCER SURVEILLANCE CONSORTIUM
(BCSC) STATISTICAL COORDINATING CENTER (C-BCSC SCC), THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL BE REQUIRED TO
FURNISH ALL THE NECESSARY SERVICES, QUALIFIED PERSONNEL, MATERIAL, EQUIPMENT, AND FACILITIES, NOT
OTHERWISE PROVIDED BY THE CONTRACT BREAST CANCER SURVEILLANCE CONSORTIUM STATISTICAL
COORDINATING CENTER AS NEEDED TO PERFORM THE STATEMENT OF WORK.
SCOPE:
THE MAJOR OBJECTIVE OF A SUBCONTRACT TO THE C-BCSC SCC DATA RESOURCE IS TO ASSIST IN THE
SHARING OF DATA STORED WITHIN THE CURRENT BCSC DATABASE AND IMPROVE ITS CAPACITY TO SUPPORT
USE OF THE DATA BY THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. TO ENSURE VALID DATA INTERPRETATION THE
SUBCONTRACTOR WILL MAINTAIN DATA USE AGREEMENTS WITH THE C-BCSC SCC TO AID IN CLARIFYING SITE SPECIFIC
DATA IN THE POOLED DATABASE.
SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS:
PROJECT AREA 1. PARTICIPATION IN BCSC POOLED DATABASE
THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN THE SCSC POOLED DATABASE THROUGH THE FOLLOWING
ACTIVITIES:
A. PROVIDE ACCESS TO THE EXISTING SITE-SPECIFIC DATA.
B. ENSURE THAT PROPER ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORIZATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS ARE IN PLACE WHICH
MAY INCLUDE, BUT MAY NOT BE LIMITED TO, IRS APPROVALS, CERTIFICATES OF CONFIDENTIALITY,
HIPAA CERTIFICATIONS, AND CERTIFICATIONS FOR RESEARCH ON HUMAN SUBJECTS. RECORDS OF
THESE APPROVALS, CERTIFICATIONS, AND OR TRAININGS SHALL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE C-SCSC
SCC UPON REQUEST.
C. WITHIN THE LIMITS OF THE SUBCONTRACTOR BUDGET AND THE AVAILABILITY OF THE DATA, ASSIST THE
C-SCSC SCC IN UNDERSTANDING PREVIOUSLY UNUSED VARIABLES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED
TO: CORRECTING DATA ELEMENTS THAT ARE INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, CONTAIN IMPOSSIBLE VALUES,
OR ARE MISSING. IT IS UNDERSTOOD THAT THE SUBCONTRACTORS MAY NOT BE ABLE TO COLLECT NEW
DATA FROM THEIR RADIOLOGY FACILITIES TO ADDRESS PROBLEMS THAT MAY EXIST IN A VARIABLE, BUT
THAT THEY WILL PURSUE THE BEST AVAILABLE REMEDY.
PROJECT AREA 2. SCSC STEERING COMMITTEE
THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT THE WORK WITH THE SCSC STEERING COMMITTEE COMPOSED OF
SCSC INVESTIGATORS THE C-BCSC SCC, AND THE NCI COTR IN THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES:
A. PARTICIPATE IN REGULAR 1.5 HOUR MONTHLY CONFERENCE CALLS FOR STEERING COMMITTEE MEMBERS
AND PROVIDE MEETING MATERIALS AS REQUESTED BY THE C-SCSC SCC FOR DOCUMENTATION OF
THE DATA AT OR BEFORE THE MEETING.
B. PARTICIPATE IN DECISIONS REGARDING DATA REQUESTS, PROPOSED ANALYSES, DATA ISSUES AND
MEETINGS, ON THE CONFERENCE CALLS.
PROJECT AREA 3. COLLABORATION WITH THE STATISTICAL COORDINATING CENTER
A. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH THE C-8CSC SCC TO ENSURE THAT EXTERNAL INVESTIGATORS
ARE AWARE OF THIS RESEARCH RESOURCE AND ITS POTENTIAL TO AID THEM IN THEIR RESEARCH.
B. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL COMPLY WITH THE REQUIREMENTS FOR TRANSITION-IN AND TRANSITION-OUT
OF THE C-8CSC SCC. SUBCONTRACTORS SHALL PARTICIPATE IN TRANSITION-IN REQUIREMENTS BY
PARTICIPATING IN THE C-BCSC SCC'S EVALUATION OF DATA COLLECTION PROCEDURES.
PROJECT AREA 4. SECURITY AND PRIVACY
THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST THE C-BCSC SCC'S IN MEETING THE SYSTEM SECURITY PROCEDURES
TO ENSURE DETAILED PHYSICAL AND DATA SECURITY OF THE POOLED BCSC DATABASE AND PRIVATE WEBSITE,
AS WELL AS TO ENSURE CONFIDENTIALITY OF PERSONAL INFORMATION OF LIMITED DATA SETS, INCLUDING LIMITS
ON CELL SIZES IN ANALYSES.
A. ALL SUBCONTRACTOR EMPLOYEES WITH ACCESS TO THE BCSC DATA SHALL TAKE SECURITY TRAINING
COMMENSURATE WITH THEIR RESPONSIBILITIES FOR PERFORMING WORK UNDER THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF
THEIR CONTRACTUAL AGREEMENTS. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL ENSURE THAT EACH SUBCONTRACTOR
EMPLOYEE HAS COMPLETED THE ONLINE TRAINING LABELED "ENTIRE INFORMATION SECURITY AWARENESS
COURSE" WITHIN THE NIH COMPUTER SECURITY AWARENESS TRAINING MODULE LOCATED AT:
HTTP://IRTSECTRAINING.NIH.GOV/ WITHIN THIRTY (30) CALENDAR DAYS OF COMMENCING WORK ON THE CONTRACT,
AND THEREAFTER COMPLETING THE NIH-SPECIFIED FISCAL YEAR REFRESHER COURSE DURING EACH PERIOD OF
PERFORMANCE OF THE CONTRACT.
B. CONFIDENTIAL TREATMENT OF SENSITIVE INFORMATION AND COMMITMENT TO PROTECT NON PUBLIC/
SENSITIVE INFORMATION
THE INFORMATION/DATA THAT THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL BE PROVIDED, OR PROVIDING, DURING THE
PERFORMANCE OF THIS REQUIREMENT IS OF A SENSITIVE NATURE. THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL NOT
RELEASE, PUBLISH, OR DISCLOSE SENSITIVE INFORMATION TO UNAUTHORIZED PERSONNEL, AND SHALL
PROTECT SUCH INFORMATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH PROVISIONS OF THE FOLLOWING LAWS AND ANY
OTHER PERTINENT LAWS AND REGULATIONS GOVERNING THE CONFIDENTIALITY OF SENSITIVE
INFORMATION:
18 U.S.C. 641 (CRIMINAL CODE: PUBLIC MONEY, PROPERTY OR RECORDS)
18 U.S.C. 1905 (CRIMINAL CODE: DISCLOSURE OF CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION)
PUBLIC LAW 96-511 (PAPERWORK REDUCTION ACT
