SUBCONTRACTORS WILL COOPERATE WITH THE CONTRACTOR IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF CERTIFICATES OF
CONFIDENTIALITY ,
WITHIN THE LIMITS OF THE SUBCONTRACTOR BUDGET AND THE AVAILABILITY OF THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA ASSIST
THE BCSC-SCC IN UNDERSTANDING PREVIOUSLY UNUSED VARIABLES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO:

Sub-Award Description:
UWNMR SHALL PERFORM NUCLEAR MAGNETIC RESONANCE (NMR)-BASED METHODS TO DETERMINE AT LEAST THREE (3) SOLUTION STRUCTURES FROM TARGETS APPROVED BY NIAID FOR ENTRY INTO THE SSGCID PIPELINE, FROM NIAID CATEGORY A-C INFECTIOUS DISEASE ORGANISMS, AS WELL AS EMERGING AND RE-EMERGING DISEASES. THE NMR SPECTROSCOPY WILL BE MAINLY DEDICATED TO PROTEINS SMALLER THAN ~25-30 KDA THAT FAIL TO PRODUCE DIFFRACTION QUALITY CRYSTALS. THE CANDIDATE TARGETS WILL BE IDENTIFIED BY THE CENTER FOR INFECTIOUS DISEASE RESEARCH TARGET SELECTION GROUP. CANDIDATES SUITABLE FOR FURTHER EXAMINATION WILL BE IDENTIFIED FROM 1H-15N HSQC SPECTRA COLLECTED ON 15N-LABELED PROTEIN PREPARED BY UW-NMR. STANDARD TRIPLE RESONANCE EXPERIMENTS WILL BE PERFORMED TO ASSIGN THE BACKBONE AND THE SIDE CHAIN RESONANCES OF THE PROTEIN. ONCE THE RESONANCE ASSIGNMENTS ARE COMPLETE, NOE DATA CRUCIAL FOR OBTAINING DISTANCE RESTRAINS WILL BE COLLECTED. NOE ASSIGNMENTS AND STRUCTURE CALCULATIONS WILL BE PERFORMED ITERATIVELY USING COMBINED AUTOMATED AND MANUAL METHODS. THE QUALITY OF THE FINAL SET OF STRUCTURES WILL BE ASSESSED AND ONCE THE FINAL ENSEMBLE OF STRUCTURES IS FOUND TO BE SATISFACTORY, THE COORDINATES OF THE ENSEMBLE AND THE MEAN STRUCTURE WILL BE DEPOSITED IN THE PROTEIN DATA BANK (PDB; HTTP://WWW.PDB.ORG) AND IMMEDIATELY RELEASED TO THE WORLD. AT THE SAME TIME, ALL 1H, 13C AND 15N CHEMICAL SHIFT DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED WITH THE BIOMAGNETIC RESEARCH BANK (BMRB; HTTP://WWW.BMRB.WISC.EDU/). MANUSCRIPTS THAT INCLUDE A DESCRIPTION OF THESE STRUCTURES WILL BE PUBLISHED IN AS TIMELY A FASHION AS IS POSSIBLE. 

UW NMR SHALL LEAD FUNCTIONAL STUDY (FUN_11) ENTITLED, "FUNCTIONAL CHARACTERIZATION OF PFHMGB2 AND DEVELOPMENT AS A DRUG TARGET FOR THE TREATMENT OF CEREBRAL MALARIA." THE AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DISCOVER AND LATER DEVELOP A LEAD INHIBITOR COMPOUND AGAINST PFHMGB2 THAT IS EFFECTIVE IN REDUCING BRAIN SWELLING AND INCREASING THE SURVIVAL OF CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL MALARIA.
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

Sub-Awardee Name: UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY RESEARCH FOUNDATION, THE
Sub-Award Description:
UNIV OF KENTUCKY WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE HIGHLY COLLABORATIVE FUNCTIONAL STUDY (FUN_12) ENTITLED, Â€ŒTHE ROLE OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS IN NONRIBOSOMAL PEPTIDE SYNTHETASE (NRPS) ASSEMBLY-LINES Â€“ TOOLS FOR BIOSYNTHESIS/ BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL ANTIBIOTICS.Â€?
THE ROLE OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS IN NONRIBOSOMAL PEPTIDE SYNTHETASE (NRPS) ASSEMBLY-LINES Â€“ TOOLS FOR BIOSYNTHESIS/BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL ANTIBIOTICS.
MANY OF THE NATURALLY DERIVED ANTIBIOTICS IN CURRENT USE ARE COMPLEX SECONDARY METABOLITES BIOSYNTHESIZED ON NONRIBOSOMAL PEPTIDE SYNTHETASE (NRPS) Â€ŒASSEMBLY-LINESÂ€? BY BACTERIA. UNIV OF KY HAS SHOWN THAT THREE SMALL PROTEINS (MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS) IN THE NPRS SYSTEM WERE ESSENTIAL FOR THE ACTIVATION OF CONGOCIDINE, KUTZNERIDE, AND THIOCORALINE NRPS SYSTEMS, RESPECTIVELY, IN S. COELICOLOR. FURTHERMORE, UNIV KY RECENTLY FOUND THAT CO-EXPRESSION OF ONE OF THESE SMALL PROTEINS (TIOT) WITH HOMOLOGUES FROM OTHER NRPS SYSTEMS RESULTED IN A DRASTIC CHANGE IN THE BIOCHEMICAL FUNCTION OF THE COMPLEX. BY COMBINING A VARIETY OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS WITH DIFFERENT OTHER NRPS PARTNERS, IT MAY BE POSSIBLE TO CREATE A TOOLBOX FOR THE BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL PHARMACEUTICALS.  
THE AIM OF THIS FUNCTIONAL STUDY IS TO USE MTBH-LIKE PROTEINS FROM M. TUBERCULOSIS AND PURIFIED BY THE SSGCID TO EXPAND THE NRPS TOOLBOX AND DETERMINE THE STRUCTURAL BASIS DRIVING THE FUNCTIONAL VARIABILITY. SPECIFIC AIMS OF THE PROJECT ARE AS FOLLOWS:
SPECIFIC AIM 1: CONSTRUCT HETEROLOGOUS NRPS CO-EXPRESSION SYSTEMS: GENES FOR THE MTBH-LIKE PROTEINS FROM SSGCID AND CSGID RELEVANT BACTERIAL PATHOGENS WILL BE CO-EXPRESSED WITH THE S. ALBUS NRPS PROTEINS TIOK AND TION AND THE CO-EXPRESSED COMPLEXES ASSAYED FOR A WIDE RANGE OF NRPS ACTIVITIES.  THIS WORK WILL BE PERFORMED IN THE GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY. 
SPECIFIC AIM 2: DETERMINE CRYSTAL STRUCTURE OF TIOK AND TION IN COMPLEX WITH VARIOUS MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS: PURIFIED CO-EXPRESSED COMPLEXES OF PROTEINS WILL BE SHIPPED BY GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA TO SSGCID FOR PLACEMENT INTO CRYSTALLIZATION SCREENS AT BERYLLIUM. IF NECESSARY, ADDITIONAL PROTEIN EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION WILL BE DONE BY DR. BUCHKO AT PNNL. THIS WORK WILL BE PERFORMED BY BOTH THE GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA LABORATORY AND SSGCID.  
SPECIFIC AIM 3:  DETERMINE A CRYSTAL STRUCTURE FOR A MBTH-MBTB COMPLEX AND ASSAY ACTIVITY: MBTH WILL ALSO BE CO-EXPRESSED WITH THE M. TUBERCULOSIS PROTEIN (MBTB) HOMOLOGOUS TO TION WITH THE AIM OF OBTAINING A STRUCTURE OF THE PROTEIN-PROTEIN COMPLEX. CLONING, PROTEIN PURIFICATION, AND ASSAY WORK WILL BE PERFORMED IN THE GARNEAU-TSODIKOVA LABORATORY AT THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY. CRYSTALLIZATION SCREENS AND STRUCTURE DETERMINATION WILL BE PERFORMED AT BERYLLIUM AND ANY ADDITIONAL PROTEIN EXPRESSION AND PURIFICATION NEEDED WILL BE DONE BY DR. BUCHKO AT PNNL. 

OUTCOMES: THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT, A TOOLBOX FOR THE BIOENGINEERING OF NOVEL PHARMACEUTICALS, ALIGNS WITH NIAIDÂ€™S MISSION OF USING STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY TO ASSIST THE STRUCTURE-BASED DESIGN OF NOVEL ANTIMICROBIAL AGENTS.  THE ACTIVITY ASSAYS WITH MULTIPLE MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS AND TIOK AND TION WILL EXPAND THE AVAILABLE BIOENGINEERING TOOLBOX AND THE COMPLEMENTARY CRYSTAL STRUCTURES OF THE MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS WITH TIOK AND TION WILL PROVIDE A STRUCTURAL BASIS TO EXPLAIN THE MOLECULAR REACTIONS THESE COMPLEXES PERFORM AND THE ROLE OF MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS IN INFLUENCING THE BIOCHEMISTRY.  NOT ONLY WILL THE STRUCTURES OF THESE MBTH-LIKE PROTEINS WITH TIOK AND TION ASSIST THE STRUCTURE BASED DESIGN OF NOVEL BIOSYNTHESIZED ANTIBIOTICS, THE CO-EXPRESSION PROTOCOL WITH MTBH-LIKE PROTEINS MAY BE THE ONLY METHOD OF DETERMINING A STRUCTURE FOR M. TUBERCULOSIS MBTB AND SOME OF THE OTHER PROTEINS IN THE M. TUBERCULOSIS NRPS ASSEMBLY-LINE THAT ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR PRODUCING SIDEROPHORES.  THE STRUCTURES OF THESE LATER COMPLEXES WILL ASSIST THE STRUCTURE-BASED DESIGN OF ANTIBIOTICS BASED ON COMPOUNDS THAT PREVENT THE FORMATION OF THESE COMPLEXES AND THE CONSEQUENTIAL IRON-STARVATION OF M. TUBERCULOSIS FOLLOWING INFECTION.
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

Sub-Award Description:
I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES
A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT.
THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. OF THE SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS TO BE STUDIED, TWO ARE MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). THE PARASITE STUDIES WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS (UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA), KING (CASE WESTERN RESERVE UNIVERSITY) AND TOLIA (WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). IN ADDITION TO THE EPITOPE MAPPING TO BE PERFORMED BY DR. TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING.
B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES
STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT.
HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS AND MURINE MABS FROM IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. MALARIA NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED USING ASSAYS INTERROGATING BOTH SPOROZOITE AND MEROZOITE STAGES OF DEVELOPMENT. QUANTITATIVE ASSAYS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE AB/AG INTERACTION STRENGTH, SPECIFICITY, AND VALENCY TO FURTHER DEVELOP CORRELATES OF PROTECTION. MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION WILL BE INTERROGATED FOR OUR MOST POTENT MABS, WHERE THE STAGE OF THE INFECTION PROCESS BLOCKED BY MABS WILL BE EVALUATED.
ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION.
II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED
A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.)
ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT.
B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS
LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION.
MAB GENERATION. LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST TARGET PATHOGENS WILL BE GENERATED. DR. ADAMS WILL COORDINATE OBTAINING EXISTING MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX ANTIGENS THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH DRS. P. DUFFY, D. KASLOW AND A. HOLDER (SEE LETTERS OF SUPPORT). MURINE PANELS OF MABS WILL BE GENERATED DR. ADAMS (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A MINIMUM OF TEN MURINE ANTIBODIES TO TWO ANTIGENS PER YEAR WILL BE OBTAINED THROUGH COLLABORATIONS OR GENERATED.
EPITOPE VALIDATION. A PRIMARY GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A FRAMEWORK RELATING B CELLS EPITOPES WITH AB BINDING AND NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY. TO ASSESS NEUTRALIZATION BY MABS TO P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX, DR. ADAMS HAS DEVELOPED NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING MALARIA SPOROZOITES OR MEROZOITES. NEUTRALIZATION OF P. FALCIPARUM SPOROZOITES WILL BE EXAMINED BY DR. ADAMS IN ONE OF THREE ASSAYS. DR. ADAMS WILL PERFORM P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX BLOOD-STAGE MEROZOITE NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS USING ESTABLISHED ASSAYS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR NEUTRALIZATION IN SPOROZOITE OR MEROZOITE ASSAYS PER YEAR.
MECHANISMS OF AB PROTECTION. A KEY QUESTION FOR PARASITES IS AT WHAT STAGE OF INFECTION/DEVELOPMENT AB NEUTRALIZATION IS ACHIEVED. DIRECT MALARIA PARASITE ANTIGEN BINDING ASSAYS TO EXAMINE MAB BLOCKADE OF AG BINDING TO HOST-CELLS AND/OR COGNATE RECEPTORS, AND THE EFFECT OF MABS ON MEROZOITE AND SPOROZOITE DEVELOPMENT WILL BE EVALUATED BY DR. ADAMS. A MINIMUM OF TEN ANTIBODIES WILL BE EVALUATED IN THESE ASSAYS PER YEAR.
DATA MANAGEMENT AND EPITOPE SUBMISSION. THIS CONTRACT WILL GENERATE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL DATA AND RESOURCES. A DATABASE AT WU WILL CATALOG THE DATA GENERATED IN ALL OF THE CONTRACT GROUPS, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO: AB POTENCY IN NEUTRALIZATION ASSAYS; AB VARIABLE DOMAIN SEQUENCES; AG RECOGNIZED; EXPRESSION VECTORS CONSTRUCTED; PROGRESS OF AB AND AG PRODUCTION; AB/AG BINDING AFFINITY AND KINETICS; PROGRESS OF YEAST SURFACE DISPLAY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF MASS SPECTROMETRY EXPERIMENTS; PROGRESS OF CRYSTALLOGRAPHY EXPERIMENTS; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY CORE STRATEGIES; EPITOPE RESIDUES DEFINED BY ALTERNATE STRATEGIES; AND RESULTS FROM AB MECHANISM OF PROTECTION STUDIES. DR. ADAMS WILL PROVIDE ALL DATA FOR DEPOSITION TO THE WU DATABASE.
ALTERNATE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES. IN ADDITION TO THE CORE EPITOPE MAPPING STRATEGIES TO BE PERFORMED BY DRS. FREMONT, GROSS AND TOLIA, OUR COLLABORATIVE TEAM HAS EXPERTISE WITH A VARIETY OF COMPLEMENTARY METHODS THAT CAN BE USED AS NEEDED. B CELL EPITOPES MAY BE MAPPED BY PHAGE DISPLAY TECHNOLOGY, A TECHNIQUE SUCCESSFULLY APPLIED BY DR. ADAMS.
C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS
IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE.
HUMAN SUBJECTS INVOLVEMENT, CHARACTERISTICS AND DESIGN
HUMAN: THIS PROJECT WILL OBTAIN HUMAN BLOOD FOR: 1) IMMUNE SERUM ANTIBODIES TO IDENTIFY AND
CHARACTERIZE EPITOPES; 2) PLASMODIUM VIVAX FOR EX VIVO INVASION ASSAYS AND DNA TO ANALYZE
GENETIC DIVERSITY OF DBP; AND 3) UNINFECTED RED BLOOD CELLS (NORMOCYTES, RETICULOCYTES) FOR IN VITRO
BINDING ASSAYS AND EX VIVO INVASION ASSAYS.

ANIMAL: USF COMPARATIVE MEDICINE MAINTAINS AN ANIMAL CARE AND USE PROGRAM IS FULLY
AAALAC ACCREDITED, AS ACCREDITED UNIT #000434. VETERINARIANS AND STAFF PROVIDE
OVERSIGHT OF ANIMAL HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, GUIDANCE AND ASSISTANCE AND EQUIPMENT AND
ROOM SANITATION. ASSOCIATED WITH GHIDR VECTOR BORNE PATHOGEN LAB ARE BSL1 AND BSL2
ANIMAL FACILITIES WITHIN IDRB, COMBINED SPACE WITH PREP ROOM AND AUTOCLAVE IS
APPROXIMATELY 800 SQ. FT., THAT ARE CAPABLE OF SUPPORTING MOST OF LABORATORY ANIMAL
RESEARCH NEEDS OF THE ONGOING PROJECTS.

ALL WORK PERFORMED UNDER THIS CONTRACT WILL BE REPORTED TO THE PROJECT MANAGER AND PROGRAM DIRECTOR AT WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY ON A QUARTERLY BASIS.
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health

THE USE OF CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM MONOVALENTLY IMMUNIZED INDIVIDUALS IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT FOR DENV-4 AND JEV, AS IN ENDEMIC REGIONS THESE VIRUSES CO-CIRCULATE WITH OTHER FLAVIVIRUSES (E.G., OTHER DENV SEROTYPES AND YELLOW FEVER VIRUS), WHICH CAN SKEW THE ANTIBODY REPERTOIRE TOWARDS MORE CROSS-REACTIVE AND LESS NEUTRALIZING ABS.
MAB TECHNOLOGIES. THE CROWE LAB HAVE SEVERAL B CELL TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL BE USED IN THIS PROJECT. ONE STRATEGY IS TO GENERATE HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS FROM CIRCULATING B CELLS USING AN ELECTROFUSION TECHNIQUE THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND OPTIMIZED. ARGUABLY, THIS APPROACH IS THE HIGHEST EFFICIENCY TECHNIQUE FOR ISOLATING HUMAN CLONES WITH NATURALLY MATCHED HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAIN GENES EVER REPORTED. THE CROWE LAB HAS GENERATED THOUSANDS OF VIRUS-SPECIFIC B CELL LINES AND MABS TO INFLUENZA, DENV, RSV, MPV, HIV, WEST NILE VIRUS AND OTHERS. THE EFFICIENCY OF THIS METHOD ALLOWED FOR GENERATION OF HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS TO THE 1918 H1N1 PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS FROM ~ 100 YEAR OLD SURVIVORS, IN WHOM THE AVERAGE CIRCULATING FREQUENCY OF SPECIFIC B CELLS SPECIFIC WAS 1 IN 4 X 106 CELLS. 
HYBRIDOMA FORMATION. THE CROWE LAB WILL THAW CRYOPRESERVED PBMC AND ISOLATE CELLS USING A FICOLL-HYPAQUE DENSITY GRADIENT METHOD. HUMAN LYMPHOCYTES WILL BE STIMULATED AND TRANSFORMED AFTER INCUBATION WITH EBV SUBSTRAIN B95.8, THE TLR AGONIST CPG ODN 2006 (2.5 ÂΜG/ML; INVIVOGEN), 10 ÂΜM OF CHK2 INHIBITOR II (SIGMA C3742), AND 1 ÂΜG/ML CYCLOSPORIN A. CELLS ARE PLATED IN 384-WELL TISSUE CULTURE PLATES AND MONITORED FOR TRANSFORMATION. TYPICALLY, 50 TO 80 COLONIES FORM PER WELL, WITH ROBUST AB SECRETION.
SCREENING FOR VIRUS-SPECIFIC AB LINES. SUPERNATANTS FROM WELLS CONTAINING EBV-TRANSFORMED LYMPHOBLASTOID CELL LINES (LCL) ARE SCREENED IN THE CROWE LABORATORY FOR VIRUS (RVFV, DENV-4, JEV) NEUTRALIZATION (ATTENUATED STRAINS ONLY) OR BINDING ACTIVITY IN ELISAS AGAINST A PANEL OF VIRAL ANTIGENS (RECOMBINANT SOLUBLE PROTEINS (GC, GN, E PROTEINS), OR INACTIVATED WHOLE VIRUS (RVFV STRAIN MP-12, DENV-4 STRAIN 1036, OR JEV STRAIN 14-14-2). CONCURRENTLY, THE CROWE LAB WILL SEND BY OVERNIGHT EXPRESS SHIPPING AN ALIQUOT OF SUPERNATANT FOR TESTING THE NEXT DAY IN A VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY USING LIVE VIRULENT WILD-TYPE RVFV (AT VGTI IN THE ROSS LABORATORY) DENV-4 (DIAMOND LABORATORY) AND JEV (DIAMOND LABORATORY). POSITIVE WELLS IN ANY OF THE ASSAYS ARE SELECTED FOR EXPANSION AND FUSION. 
ELECTROFUSION. EBV-TRANSFORMED LCL SECRETE HUMAN ABS, BUT ARE QUITE UNSTABLE AND DIFFICULT TO CLONE. LCLS SECRETING VIRUS-SPECIFIC MABS ARE FUSED WITH HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS TO FORM HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS, WHICH ARE CONSIDERABLY MORE STABLE. THE SYSTEM USED IS A PROGRAMMABLE ELECTROFUSION SOURCE (CYTOPULSE PA-4000/PA-101). HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS AND EBV-TRANSFORMED HUMAN B CELLS ARE WASHED WITH RPMI-1640 AND CYTOFUSION MEDIUM. LARGE VOLUME FUSION CHAMBERS ARE COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE AND INTERFACE WELL WITH THIS UNIT. THE KEY TO THE FUSION IS BRINGING THE TWO CELL TYPES INTO CLOSE PHYSICAL CONTACT. AFTER FUSION, CELLS ARE ALLOWED TO RECOVER IN THE FUSION ELECTRODE FOR 30 MINUTES, HARVESTED, AND THEN WASHED ONCE WITH RPMI-1640 AT ROOM TEMPERATURE PRIOR TO PLATING IN SELECTION PLATES. 
HYBRIDOMA SELECTION AND CLONING. FUSED CELLS ARE SEEDED INTO 384-WELL PLATES IN COMPLETE MEDIUM CONTAINING HAT AND OUABAIN. AFTER FIVE DAYS OF CULTURE, CELLS ARE FED WITH FRESH MEDIUM CONTAINING HYPOXANTHINE/THYMIDINE OR HT. WE USED A SERIES OF STEMCELL TECHNOLOGIES MEDIA FOR THESE PROCEDURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE CLONACELLÂ®-HY MEDIUM E FOR GROWTH AND EXPANSION. AFTER INITIAL SCREENING FOR HUMAN AB PRODUCTION BY ELISA, THE HYBRIDOMA CELLS FROM POSITIVE WELLS ARE EXPANDED INTO 96- AND THEN 24-WELL PLATES AND CULTURED IN COMPLETE MEDIUM AND THEN HYBRIDOMA CELLS ARE SEEDED IN 96-WELL PLATES AT 0.3 CELL-PER-WELL DENSITY. LIMITING DILUTION IS PERFORMED TWICE TO ENSURE THAT HYBRIDOMA CLONES ARE GENERATED. ALTERNATIVELY, WE CAN SINGLE-CELL SORT THE LINES ON A FACSARIA III FLOW OR USE A CLONEPIX INSTRUMENT. CULTURE SUPERNATANTS ARE SCREENED BY ELISA FOR HUMAN IGG AND ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC ABS. THE COATING ANTIGENS INCLUDE INACTIVATED VIRUSES, LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS PARTICLES, AND RECOMBINANT ENVELOPE GLYCOPROTEINS. 
MAB PREPARATIONS. HYBRIDOMA CELL LINES WILL BE ADAPTED TO SERUM-FREE MEDIUM. SUPERNATANTS OF HIGH-DENSITY CULTURES WILL BE PRODUCED IN CELLINE DEVICES (BD BIOSCIENCES). PURIFIED AND CONCENTRATED PREPARATIONS OF EACH MAB WILL BE PREPARED BY FPLC USING PROTEIN G RESIN ON AN AKTA INSTRUMENT FOLLOWED BY BUFFER EXCHANGE USING ULTRA CENTRIFUGAL FILTER DEVICES. FOR LARGER SCALE PREPARATIONS (E.G., 50 TO 100 MG LOTS), WE WILL SCALE THE CELL CULTURE UP TO 25 L USING A WAVE BIOREACTOR. VOLUME WILL BE INITIALLY REDUCED USING A GE QUIXSTAND LABORATORY-SCALE SEPARATION SYSTEM THAT USES CROSS-FLOW FILTRATION CARTRIDGES. THIS PROCEDURE IS FOLLOWED BY FPLC PURIFICATION. WE WILL USE QUANTITATIVE ELISAS TO DEFINE THE FINAL CONCENTRATION OF MABS. 

C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS
IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE.

TOLIA, A SECOND MAJOR GOAL OF OUR PROJECT IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF CORRELATES RELATING B CELL EPITOPES WITH AB NEUTRALIZATION POTENCY AND AG BINDING THAT WILL BE PERFORMED BY DRS. ADAMS AND KING.

STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT.

Sub-Award Description:
I. BACKGROUND INFORMATION AND OBJECTIVES
A. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
PROVIDE A GENERAL, NON-TECHNICAL BRIEF SUMMARY OF THE REQUIREMENT.
THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO IDENTIFY AND FUNCTIONALLY ASSESS B CELL EPITOPES FOR TARGETED VIRAL AND PARASITIC ANTIGENS. SIX DISTINCT ARTHROPOD-BORNE PATHOGENS OF HUMAN WILL BE STUDIED: TWO FLAVIVIRUSES (DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 AND JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS), TWO BUNYAVIRUSES (RIFT VALLEY FEVER AND OROPOUCHE VIRUSES) AND TWO MALARIA PARASITES (P. FALCIPARUM AND P. VIVAX). A KEY REQUIREMENT FOR THE SUCCESS OF EPITOPE DISCOVERY IS THE AVAILABILITY OF LARGE PANELS OF MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS). WE HAVE DEVELOPED A STRONG PLAN FOR THE GENERATION OF HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR IMMUNIZATION OF OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. 
B. PHASE II TECHNICAL OBJECTIVES
STATE THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES AND LIST THE ANTICIPATED END RESULTS OF THE PROPOSED PHASE II EFFORT.
LARGE PANELS OF NEUTRALIZING MABS AGAINST TARGET VIRUSES WILL BE GENERATED BY DR. JAMES CROWE. HUMAN MABS FROM NATURAL INFECTIONS OR VACCINE TRIALS WILL BE DEVELOPED AGAINST RIFT VALLEY FEVER VIRUS (RVFV), DENGUE VIRUS SEROTYPE 4 (DENV-4), JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS (JEV) AND OROPOUCHE VIRUS.  
ALL DATA GENERATED BY THIS CONTRACT WILL BE DEPOSITED IN RELEVANT DATABASES: EPITOPES WILL BE SUBMITTED TO THE IEDB, STRUCTURAL DATA WILL BE DEPOSITED TO THE PDB, AND FUNCTIONAL DATA WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE IN A DEFINED ACCESSIBLE FORMAT. AT THE COMPLETION OF THIS CONTRACT, A LARGE NUMBER OF NOVEL AND SIGNIFICANT DELIVERABLES ARE EXPECTED. THESE INCLUDE B CELL EPITOPES, ATOMIC STRUCTURES OF AB/AG COMPLEXES, RECOMBINANT AGS, PANELS OF HUMAN AND MURINE MABS, KINETIC AND THERMODYNAMIC PARAMETERS OF BINDING, FUNCTIONAL CORRELATES OF NEUTRALIZATION, AND MECHANISMS OF AB-MEDIATED PROTECTION.
II. SERVICES TO BE PERFORMED
A. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INDEPENDENTLY PERFORM ALL WORK AND FURNISH ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND SERVICES (EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SPECIFIED IN THE CONTRACT.)
ALL WORK WILL BE MONITORED BY THE GOVERNMENT PROJECT OFFICER IDENTIFIED IN SECTION G OF THE CONTRACT.
B. SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS
LIST ALL TASKS IN A LOGICAL SEQUENCE TO PRECISELY DESCRIBE WHAT IS EXPECTED OF THE CONTRACTOR IN PERFORMANCE OF THE WORK. TASKS SHOULD CONTAIN DETAIL TO (1) ESTABLISH PARAMETERS FOR THE PROJECT, (2) KEEP THE EFFORT FOCUSED ON MEETING THE OBJECTIVES, (3) DESCRIBE END PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES, AND (4) DESCRIBE PERIODIC/FINAL REPORTS REQUIRED TO MONITOR WORK PROGRESS UNDER THE CONTRACT. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY PROPRIETARY INFORMATION.
A CRITICAL ELEMENT OF OUR PROPOSAL IS THE GENERATION OF LARGE PANELS OF MABS AGAINST OUR TARGET PATHOGENS. HUMAN MABS AGAINST FLAVIVIRUS AND BUNYAVIRUS TARGETS WILL BE DEVELOPED IN THE CROWE LAB. THE MABS FOR RVFV THAT WILL BE MAPPED IN THIS CONTRACT ARE BEING ISOLATED AS PART OF ONGOING RESEARCH IN COLLABORATION OF TED ROSS, PHD OF VGTI IN FLORIDA. THE DENV-4 HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF SUBJECTS IMMUNIZED WITH A LIVE-ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE THAT HAS BEEN USED SUCCESSFULLY IN HUMAN TRIALS IN COLLABORATION WITH A. DURBIN AND S. WHITEHEAD. THE JEV HUMAN MABS WILL BE ISOLATED FROM PBMCS OF VOLUNTEERS WHO HAVE RECEIVED A LIVE-ATTENUATED OR INACTIVATED JEV VACCINE IN COLLABORATION WITH S. THOMAS AND FROM CONVALESCENT PBMCS FROM SUBJECTS INFECTED WITH JEV IN THE FIELD IN COLLABORATION WITH C. SIMMONS. FOR THIS CONTRACT, THE CROWE LABORATORY WILL SUPPLY HIGHLY PURIFIED IGG PREPARATIONS OF HUMAN MABS WITH KNOWN FUNCTIONAL ACTIVITY. THE TEXT BELOW DESCRIBES A PLAN FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE MABS.
SOURCE OF HUMAN B CELLS. NATURAL INFECTION. FOR SOME OF THE VIRUSES TARGETED FOR HUMAN MAB PRODUCTION (JEV, RVFV), SOME OF THE SAMPLES WILL BE OBTAINED FROM PERIPHERAL BLOOD CELLS OF OTHERWISE HEALTHY DONORS WHO SUFFERED ACUTE AND CONFIRMED VIRAL INFECTION. THIS WILL BE COORDINATED BY DR. CROWE AND COLLABORATORS (RVFV: DR. MARIETJIE VENTER, UNIVERSITY OF PRETORIA; JEV: DR. CAMERON SIMMONS, OXFORD UNIVERSITY CLINICAL RESEARCH UNIT, VIETNAM). CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM SEVERAL IMMUNE DONORS WILL BE TRANSFERRED IN A COMPLETELY DE-IDENTIFIED FASHION TO THE VANDERBILT VACCINE CENTER IN THE U.S. FOR THESE STUDIES. IMMUNIZATION. PBMCS ARE AVAILABLE FROM A LARGE NUMBER OF VACCINE RECIPIENTS WHO HAVE RECEIVED EITHER THE INACTIVATED RVFV VACCINE OR THE LIVE ATTENUATED MP-12 STRAIN AT USAMRIID IN MARYLAND, A LIVE ATTENUATED MONOVALENT DENV-4 VACCINE (NIH AND JOHNS HOPKINS), OR INACTIVATED OR LIVE-ATTENUATED JEV (WRAIR). WITH THE HELP OF OUR COLLABORATORS, SUBJECTS WITH HIGH TITER NEUTRALIZING POLYCLONAL ABS WILL BE IDENTIFIED AND, DR. CROWE WILL OBTAIN DE-IDENTIFIED CELLS FROM VACCINEES. THE USE OF CRYOPRESERVED PBMCS FROM MONOVALENTLY IMMUNIZED INDIVIDUALS IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT FOR DENV-4 AND JEV, AS IN ENDEMIC REGIONS THESE VIRUSES CO-CIRCULATE WITH OTHER FLAVIVIRUSES (E.G., OTHER DENV SEROTYPES AND YELLOW FEVER VIRUS), WHICH CAN SKEW THE ANTIBODY REPERTOIRE TOWARDS MORE CROSS-REACTIVE AND LESS NEUTRALIZING ABS.
MAB TECHNOLOGIES. THE CROWE LAB HAVE SEVERAL B CELL TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL BE USED IN THIS PROJECT. ONE STRATEGY IS TO GENERATE HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS FROM CIRCULATING B CELLS USING AN ELECTROFUSION TECHNIQUE THAT HAS BEEN VALIDATED AND OPTIMIZED. ARGUABLY, THIS APPROACH IS THE HIGHEST EFFICIENCY TECHNIQUE FOR ISOLATING HUMAN CLONES WITH NATURALLY MATCHED HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAIN GENES EVER REPORTED. THE CROWE LAB HAS GENERATED THOUSANDS OF VIRUS-SPECIFIC B CELL LINES AND MABS TO INFLUENZA, DENV, RSV, MPV, HIV, WEST NILE VIRUS AND OTHERS. THE EFFICIENCY OF THIS METHOD ALLOWED FOR GENERATION OF HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS TO THE 1918 H1N1 PANDEMIC INFLUENZA VIRUS FROM ~ 100 YEAR OLD SURVIVORS, IN WHOM THE AVERAGE CIRCULATING FREQUENCY OF SPECIFIC B CELLS SPECIFIC WAS 1 IN 4 X 106 CELLS. 
HYBRIDOMA FORMATION. THE CROWE LAB WILL THAW CRYOPRESERVED PBMC AND ISOLATE CELLS USING A FICOLL-HYPAQUE DENSITY GRADIENT METHOD. HUMAN LYMPHOCYTES WILL BE STIMULATED AND TRANSFORMED AFTER INCUBATION WITH EBV SUBSTRAIN B95.8, THE TLR AGONIST CPG ODN 2006 (2.5 ÂΜG/ML; INVIVOGEN), 10 ÂΜM OF CHK2 INHIBITOR II (SIGMA C3742), AND 1 ÂΜG/ML CYCLOSPORIN A. CELLS ARE PLATED IN 384-WELL TISSUE CULTURE PLATES AND MONITORED FOR TRANSFORMATION. TYPICALLY, 50 TO 80 COLONIES FORM PER WELL, WITH ROBUST AB SECRETION.
SCREENING FOR VIRUS-SPECIFIC AB LINES. SUPERNATANTS FROM WELLS CONTAINING EBV-TRANSFORMED LYMPHOBLASTOID CELL LINES (LCL) ARE SCREENED IN THE CROWE LABORATORY FOR VIRUS (RVFV, DENV-4, JEV) NEUTRALIZATION (ATTENUATED STRAINS ONLY) OR BINDING ACTIVITY IN ELISAS AGAINST A PANEL OF VIRAL ANTIGENS (RECOMBINANT SOLUBLE PROTEINS (GC, GN, E PROTEINS), OR INACTIVATED WHOLE VIRUS (RVFV STRAIN MP-12, DENV-4 STRAIN 1036, OR JEV STRAIN 14-14-2). CONCURRENTLY, THE CROWE LAB WILL SEND BY OVERNIGHT EXPRESS SHIPPING AN ALIQUOT OF SUPERNATANT FOR TESTING THE NEXT DAY IN A VIRUS NEUTRALIZATION ASSAY USING LIVE VIRULENT WILD-TYPE RVFV (AT VGTI IN THE ROSS LABORATORY) DENV-4 (DIAMOND LABORATORY) AND JEV (DIAMOND LABORATORY). POSITIVE WELLS IN ANY OF THE ASSAYS ARE SELECTED FOR EXPANSION AND FUSION. 
ELECTROFUSION. EBV-TRANSFORMED LCL SECRETE HUMAN ABS, BUT ARE QUITE UNSTABLE AND DIFFICULT TO CLONE. LCLS SECRETING VIRUS-SPECIFIC MABS ARE FUSED WITH HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS TO FORM HUMAN HYBRIDOMAS, WHICH ARE CONSIDERABLY MORE STABLE. THE SYSTEM USED IS A PROGRAMMABLE ELECTROFUSION SOURCE (CYTOPULSE PA-4000/PA-101). HMMA2.5 MYELOMA CELLS AND EBV-TRANSFORMED HUMAN B CELLS ARE WASHED WITH RPMI-1640 AND CYTOFUSION MEDIUM. LARGE VOLUME FUSION CHAMBERS ARE COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE AND INTERFACE WELL WITH THIS UNIT. THE KEY TO THE FUSION IS BRINGING THE TWO CELL TYPES INTO CLOSE PHYSICAL CONTACT. AFTER FUSION, CELLS ARE ALLOWED TO RECOVER IN THE FUSION ELECTRODE FOR 30 MINUTES, HARVESTED, AND THEN WASHED ONCE WITH RPMI-1640 AT ROOM TEMPERATURE PRIOR TO PLATING IN SELECTION PLATES. 
HYBRIDOMA SELECTION AND CLONING. FUSED CELLS ARE SEEDED INTO 384-WELL PLATES IN COMPLETE MEDIUM CONTAINING HAT AND OUABAIN. AFTER FIVE DAYS OF CULTURE, CELLS ARE FED WITH FRESH MEDIUM CONTAINING HYPOXANTHINE/THYMIDINE OR HT. WE USED A SERIES OF STEMCELL TECHNOLOGIES MEDIA FOR THESE PROCEDURES, MOST IMPORTANTLY THE CLONACELLÂ®-HY MEDIUM E FOR GROWTH AND EXPANSION. AFTER INITIAL SCREENING FOR HUMAN AB PRODUCTION BY ELISA, THE HYBRIDOMA CELLS FROM POSITIVE WELLS ARE EXPANDED INTO 96- AND THEN 24-WELL PLATES AND CULTURED IN COMPLETE MEDIUM AND THEN HYBRIDOMA CELLS ARE SEEDED IN 96-WELL PLATES AT 0.3 CELL-PER-WELL DENSITY. LIMITING DILUTION IS PERFORMED TWICE TO ENSURE THAT HYBRIDOMA CLONES ARE GENERATED. ALTERNATIVELY, WE CAN SINGLE-CELL SORT THE LINES ON A FACSARIA III FLOW OR USE A CLONEPIX INSTRUMENT. CULTURE SUPERNATANTS ARE SCREENED BY ELISA FOR HUMAN IGG AND ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC ABS. THE COATING ANTIGENS INCLUDE INACTIVATED VIRUSES, LIVE ATTENUATED VIRUS PARTICLES, AND RECOMBINANT ENVELOPE GLYCOPROTEINS. 
MAB PREPARATIONS. HYBRIDOMA CELL LINES WILL BE ADAPTED TO SERUM-FREE MEDIUM. SUPERNATANTS OF HIGH-DENSITY CULTURES WILL BE PRODUCED IN CELLINE DEVICES (BD BIOSCIENCES). PURIFIED AND CONCENTRATED PREPARATIONS OF EACH MAB WILL BE PREPARED BY FPLC USING PROTEIN G RESIN ON AN AKTA INSTRUMENT FOLLOWED BY BUFFER EXCHANGE USING ULTRA CENTRIFUGAL FILTER DEVICES. FOR LARGER SCALE PREPARATIONS (E.G., 50 TO 100 MG LOTS), WE WILL SCALE THE CELL CULTURE UP TO 25 L USING A WAVE BIOREACTOR. VOLUME WILL BE INITIALLY REDUCED USING A GE QUIXSTAND LABORATORY-SCALE SEPARATION SYSTEM THAT USES CROSS-FLOW FILTRATION CARTRIDGES. THIS PROCEDURE IS FOLLOWED BY FPLC PURIFICATION. WE WILL USE QUANTITATIVE ELISAS TO DEFINE THE FINAL CONCENTRATION OF MABS. 

C. HUMAN SUBJECTS AND/OR ANIMALS
IF THE RESEARCH PLAN INCLUDES THE USE OF HUMAN SUBJECTS OR ANIMALS REFER TO PARAGRAPHS IV. I Â€“ O. OF THE PHS SOLICITATION FOR FURTHER GUIDANCE.
HUMANS: DR. CROWE WILL BE CREATING HUMAN MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES. THERE WILL BE NO IDENTIFIERS LINKED TO THE DATA BEING TRANSFERRED TO WASHINGTON UNIVERSITY.
PLEASE NOTE: ANY CHANGES TO THIS PROPOSAL THAT MAY ALTER ITS "NON-HUMAN"STATUS SHOULD BE PRESENTED TO THE IRB FOR APPROVAL PRIOR TO IMPLEMENTATION OF THE CHANGES. IN ACCORDANCE WITH IRB POLICY III.J, AMENDMENTS WILL BE ACCEPTED UP TO ONE YEAR FROM THE DATE OF APPROVAL. IF SUCH CHANGES ARE REQUESTED BEYOND THIS TIME FRAME, SUBMISSION OF A NEW PROPOSAL IS REQUIRED.

Sub-Award Description:
BREAST CANCER SURVEILLANCE CONSORTIUM DATA RESOURCE
INDEPENDENTLY AND NOT AS AN AGENT OF THE BREAST CANCER SURVEILLANCE CONSORTIUM (BCSC) DATA
RESOURCE STATISTICAL COORDINATING CENTER (BCSC-SCC), THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL BE REQUIRED TO
FURNISH ALL THE NECESSARY SERVICES, QUALIFIED PERSONNEL, MATERIAL, EQUIPMENT, AND FACILITIES , NOT
OTHERWISE PROVIDED BY THE BCSC-SCC, AS NEEDED TO PERFORM THE STATEMENT OF WORK.
SCOPE:
THE MAJOR OBJECTIVE OF THIS SUBCONTRACT IS TO ASSIST IN THE SHARING OF EXISTING DATA STORED WITHIN
THE CURRENT BCSC POOLED DATABASE AND IMPROVE ITS CAPACITY TO SUPPORT USE OF THIS POOLED DATA
BY THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL DO THIS BY PROVIDING APPROVAL FOR DATA
SHARING, AND BY RESPONDING TO QUERIES FROM THE BCSC-SCC DATA RESOURCE TO HELP THEM CLEAN
THE POOLED DATA. IF THE SUBCONTRACTOR IS COVERED UNDER HIPAA, IT WILL MAINTAIN DATA USE
AGREEMENTS (DUAS) TO ENSURE VALID DATA INTERPRETATION WITH THE BCSC-SCC. THE DUAS ARE
REQUIRED IN THE EVENT THAT THE SUBCONTRACTOR NEEDS TO ACCESS ITS SITE-SPECIFIC DATA IN ORDER TO
SEND A CORRECTED DATASET BACK TO THE BCSC-SCC DATA RESOURCE IN ORDER TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY
OF THE POOLED DATABASE.
THERE ARE THREE DATA SOURCES FOR THIS CONTRACT: 1} THE POOLED DATA; 2) THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA; 3)
THE CORRECTED SITE-SPECIFIC DATA. THE SUBCONTRACTOR WILL NEVER HAVE ACCESS TO THE DATABASE
CONTAINING THE POOLED DATA. THIS CONTRACT DOES NOT COVER THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, BUT DOES COVER
CORRECTIONS (I.E., CORRECTED DATASETS) OF SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, WHICH WILL BE SENT BACK TO THE BCSC-SCC,
AND THE BCSC-SCC STAFF WILL REPLACE THE ERRONEOUS DATA ELEMENTS WITH THE CORRECT DATA.
SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS:
PROJECT AREA 1. PARTICIPATION IN MAINTAINING DATA QUALITY OF THE BCSC POOLED DATABASE
THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL PARTICIPATE IN IMPROVING THE DATA QUALITY OF THE BCSC- POOLED DATABASE
THROUGH THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES:
A. ACCESSING SITE-SPECIFIC DATA TO SUPPLY CORRECTIONS TO THE BCSC-SCC POOLED DATASET, AS
NEEDED. THIS CONTRACT DOES NOT COVER COLLECTION OF ADDITIONAL SITE-SPECIFIC DATA, BUT DOES
COVER SUBMISSION OF CORRECTED SITE-SPECIFIC DATA TO THE BCSC-SCC. THE SUBCONTRACTOR
ONLY WILL ACCESS SITE-SPECIFIC DATA THAT IS ALREADY IN THEIR POSSESSION. THE SUBCONTRACTOR
WILL NEVER ACCESS THE DATABASE CONTAINING THE POOLED DATA.
B. ENSURE THAT PROPER ADMINISTRATIVE AUTHORIZATIONS AND CERTIFICATIONS ARE IN PLACE WHICH
MAY INCLUDE, BUT MAY NOT BE LIMITED TO, IRB APPROVALS, HIPAA CERTIFICAT IONS, AND
CERTIFICATIONS FOR RESEARCH ON HUMAN SUBJECTS. RECORDS OF THESE APPROVALS,
CERTIFICATIONS, AND OR TRAININGS SHALL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE BCSC-SCC UPON REQUEST.
SUBCONTRACTORS WILL COOPERATE WITH THE CONTRACTOR IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF CERTIFICATES OF
CONFIDENTIALITY ,
WITHIN THE LIMITS OF THE SUBCONTRACTOR BUDGET AND THE AVAILABILITY OF THE SITE-SPECIFIC DATA ASSIST
THE BCSC-SCC IN UNDERSTANDING PREVIOUSLY UNUSED VARIABLES, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO:
CORRECTING DATA ELEMENTS THAT ARE INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, CONTAIN IMPOSSIBLE VALUES, OR ARE
MISSING. IT IS UNDERSTOOD THAT THE SUBCONTRACTORS MAY NOT BE ABLE TO PROVIDE CORRECTIONS FOR
APPARENTLY ERRONEOUS DATA, BUT THAT THEY WILL, TO THE BEST OF THEIR ABILITY, ATTEMPT TO DETERMINE
NECESSARY MODIFICATIONS.
PROJECT AREA 2. BCSC STEERING COMMITTEE
THE SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT THE WORK WITH THE BCSC STEERING COMMITTEE COMPOSED OF
BCSC INVESTIGATORS THE BCSC-SCC, AND THE NCI COTR IN THE FOLLOWING ACTIVITIES:
A. PARTICIPATE IN REGULAR 1.5 HOUR MONTHLY CONFERENCE CALLS FOR STEERING COMMITTEE MEMBERS
AND PROVIDE MEETING MATERIALS AS REQUESTED BY THE BCSC-SCC FOR DOCUMENTATION OF THE
POOLED DATA AT OR BEFORE THE MEETING.
B. PARTICIPATE IN DECISIONS REGARDING POOLED DATA REQUESTS, PROPOSED ANALYSES, SITE SPECIFIC
DATA ISSUES AND MEETINGS, ON THE CONFERENCE CALLS.

Sub-Award Description:
"NOVA PROPOSED KEY PERSONNEL SUPPORT 

PROJECT MANAGER/CORPORATE MONITOR:  DANA M. YOUNG, JD. MS. YOUNG WILL OVERSEE AND MANAGE CONTRACTING MATTERS, PARTICIPATE IN COMMUNICATIONS WITH NCI DCCPS, ASSIST DR. MILLIKEN AS NEEDED IN PRIORITIZING AND PROVIDING CORPORATE RESOURCES, ATTEND CANCER CENTER MEETING IN HOUSTON, TX IN NOVEMBER TO ASSIST IN DOCUMENTING DISCUSSIONS AND NETWORKING WITH KEY CANCER CENTER REPRESENTATIVES, AND PROVIDE INPUT ON AND PERFORM QC REVIEW OF DRAFT AND FINAL REPORTS. 

SENIOR SCIENCE WRITER:  ERIN MILLIKEN, PHD. DR. MILLIKEN WILL BE THE LEAD WRITER PREPARING THE SYNTHESIS REPORT. SHE WILL COMMUNICATE WITH NCI DCCPS AS NEEDED, REVIEW CANCER CENTER SUPPLEMENT FINAL REPORTS, ATTEND CANCER CENTER MEETING IN HOUSTON, TX IN NOVEMBER, IDENTIFY KEY QUESTIONS/ISSUES REQUIRING FOLLOW-UP, CONDUCT NECESSARY FOLLOW-UP DISCUSSIONS WITH CANCER CENTER REPRESENTATIVES AND/OR GATHER ADDITIONAL INFORMATION, PREPARE SYNTHESIS REPORT OUTLINE, PREPARE DRAFT AND FINAL SYNTHESIS REPORTS FOR DELIVERY TO NCI DCCPS.  

NOVA TECHNICAL SUPPORT 

COMMUNICATE WITH NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD AS NEEDED THROUGHOUT THE PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE.  

PREPARE A WORK PLAN/TIMELINE FOR TASK PERFORMANCE, TO BE APPROVED BY NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD. 

SUBMIT MONTHLY REPORTS ON PROGRESS TO NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD. 

UPON RECEIPT, REVIEW EACH OF THE 18 CANCER CENTERS SUPPLEMENT FINAL REPORTS (APPROXIMATELY 20 PP EACH) AND IDENTIFY COMMON THEMES, ISSUES, AND OTHER VARIABLES OF INTEREST. IDENTIFY ANY QUESTIONS AND/OR GAPS IN INFORMATION REQUIRING FOLLOWUP. 

ATTEND MEETING ON NOVEMBER 5-6, 2015 IN HOUSTON, TEXAS WHERE THE 18 CANCER CENTERS AWARDED SUPPLEMENTS WILL REPORT OUT ON FINDINGS. TAKE NOTES AT THE MEETING FOR PURPOSES OF ASSISTING IN PREPARATION OF THE SYNTHESIS REPORT. 

IDENTIFY ANY ADDITIONAL QUESTIONS OR INFORMATION REQUIRED TO PREPARE A SUBSTANTIVE SYNTHESIS OF THE CANCER CENTER SUPPLEMENTS AND APPROPRIATE PERSONS TO FOLLOW UP WITH AT CANCER CENTERS. 

OBTAIN APPROVAL FROM NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD TO INITIATE CONTACT WITH APPROPRIATE PERSONS AT CANCER CENTERS.  DOCUMENT DISCUSSIONS. 

USING INFORMATION GATHERED FROM REVIEW OF SUPPLEMENT FINAL REPORTS, ATTENDANCE AT HOUSTON MEETING, AND DISCUSSIONS WITH CANCER CENTER REPRESENTATIVES, PREPARE AN OUTLINE OF REPORT FOR APPROVAL BY NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD.   

FOLLOWING APPROVAL OF SYNTHESIS REPORT OUTLINE BEGIN WRITING OF DRAFT REPORT. 

DELIVER DRAFT REPORT TO NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD ON OR ABOUT JANUARY 15, 2016. 

A NOVA EDITOR/PROOFREADER WILL EDIT THE DRAFT REPORT FOR CORRECT GRAMMAR, SPELLING, PUNCTUATION, AND TONE, AND ENSURE THAT THE DOCUMENT IS PRESENTED IN THE FORMAT AND LEVEL OF DETAIL CONSISTENT WITH AGREED-UPON REQUIREMENTS. 

NOVA WILL REVISE THE REPORT AS DEEMED NECESSARY BY NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD.  

WITHIN THE AGREED-UPON SCHEDULE, NOVA WILL DELIVER A FINAL SYNTHESIS REPORT AND ASSOCIATED SLIDE DECK TO THE NCI DCCPS TASK LEAD FOR FINAL REVIEW AND APPROVAL.  "

PREVIOUSLY DESCRIBED ALLELES, ESSENTIALLY UNIFYING THESE TWO PREVIOUSLY DISPARATE GOALS INTO
A SINGLE HIGH-RESOLUTION AND COST-EFFECTIVE ASSAY. THIS STATE-OF-THE-ART ASSAY IS AVAILABLE TODAY
AND WILL BE IMPROVED DURING THE CONTRACT. MHC CLASS II -DPA, -DPB, -DQA, -DQB, AND -DRA
ALLELES WILL BE SANGER SEQUENCED FROM 415 OF THE 715 MACAQUES. CDNA LIBRARIES FROM 15 OF
THE 715 ANIMALS WILL BE CONSTRUCTED FROM HIGH-PRIORITY ANIMALS TO FACILITATE IDENTIFICATION OF
NON-CODING REGIONS OF MHC GENES AND TO PROVIDE A RESOURCE FOR OTHERS INTERESTED IN CHARACTERIZING
GENES WITHIN THE EXTENDED MHC. ALLELES WILL BE CHARACTERIZED USING CRITERIA ESTABLISHED FOR
HLA NOMENCLATURE, WHICH WILL RESULT IN CHARACTERIZATION OF BOTH FULL-LENGTH AND PARTIAL TRANSCRIPTS
USING TECHNOLOGY AVAILABLE TODAY. WE STRONGLY BELIEVE, HOWEVER, THAT FULL-LENGTH TRANSCRIPT
ALLELE DISCOVERY IS PREFERABLE AND ATTAINABLE AND WILL AGGRESSIVELY DEVELOP TECHNOLOGIES THAT
WILL ENABLE HIGH-THROUGHPUT, FULL-LENGTH TRANSCRIPT SEQUENCING DURING THE CONTRACT PROPOSAL. 300
MHC CLASS I AND 300 MHC CLASS II PLASMID CLONES WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE SCIENTIFIC
COMMUNITY.
ALL 715 MACAQUES WILL BE EXAMINED WITH DNA MICROSATELLITE MARKERS TO DEFINE HAPLOTYPES,
WHILE AT LEAST 20 NEW MHC MICROSATELLITE MARKERS WILL BE DEFINED. SUCH MARKERS WILL ENABLE
ANY MOLECULAR BIOLOGY LABORATORY TO MHC HAPLOTYPE NHPS WITHOUT REQUIRING THE SOPHISTICATED
SEQUENCING AND INFORMATICS SKILLS NECESSARY FOR HIGH-THROUGHPUT DNA SEQUENCING. IN ADDITION,
IMMORTALIZED B CELL LINES FROM 250 OF THE 715 ANIMALS WILL BE PRODUCED AND MADE AVAILABLE TO
THE COMMUNITY TO SERVE AS CONTROLS FOR LABORATORIES INTERESTED IN DEVELOPING GENOTYPING AND HAPLOTYPING
EXPERTISE. THE COMMUNITY WILL ALSO BENEFIT FROM THE PRODUCTION OF 50 STABLE TRANSFERENT
CELL LINES EXPRESSING INDIVIDUAL MHC CLASS I OR COMBINATIONS OF MHC CLASS II A AND B ALLELES, AS
WELL AS 15 MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES SPECIFIC FOR INDIVIDUAL MHC ALLELES.
ALLELE DISCOVERY, MHC GENOTYPING, AND MHC HAPLOTYPING PROTOCOLS, ALONG WITH QUALITY CONTROL

PSC.description: SPECIAL STUDIES/ANALYSIS- MEDICAL/HEALTH

Sub-Award Description: TASK 1: RECEIVE AND REVIEW MATERIALS ABOUT THE NPSD - TRUVEN HEALTH WILL HAVE NO HOURS ALLOCATED TO THIS TASK. TASK 2: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL PREPARE TO RECEIVE EVENT-LEVEL DATA AND CONSULT WITH THE PPC ON VARIABILITY ANALYSIS FOR NON-IDENTIFIABLE EVENTS.  IN COLLABORATION WITH STANFORD UNIVERSITY, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL REVIEW, REVISE OR DEVELOP NEW TABLE LAYOUTS FOR AGGREGATED DATA, AND DESIGN ANALYTIC PLANS FOR EVENT LEVEL ANALYSES (ESTIMATED 500 TABLES). TRUVEN HEALTH WILL REVIEW DISSEMINATION STRATEGY, DRAFT RECOMMENDATIONS FOR CHANGES TO THE AHRQ COMMON FORMATS BASED ON ANALYSES. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL PARTICIPATE IN ONE HOUR INTERNAL WEEKLY CALLS AND ADDITIONAL CALLS AS REQUIRED. TASK 3: ANALYZE DATA ON TRENDS IN PATIENT SAFETY EVENTS AND PATTERNS OF HEALTH CARE ERROR  - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL DESIGN ANALYTIC PLAN FOR TASK 3, DEVELOP 160 PROVIDER TABLES, DEVELOP GRAPHICS FOR TABLES, AND CREATE BULLET TEXT FOR 160 TABLES. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL DEVELOP TRENDS FROM EXISTING EXTERNAL PATIENT SAFETY DATA, SUCH AS THE HCUP DATABASES, OASIS, MDS, NSQUIP, OR QSRS. FOR THESE SOURCES, THEY WILL DEVELOP APPROXIMATELY 70 TABLES, WITH BULLETS. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL DEVELOP MULTIVARIATE TRENDS ANALYSES AND CREATE BULLETED TEXT FOR TABLES. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL REVIEW TABLES, GRAPHICS AND BULLETS CREATED BY OTHER SUBCONTRACTOR(S). TASK 4: REPORT ON PATIENT SAFETY EVENTS IN THE NATIONAL HEALTHCARE QUALITY AND DISPARITIES REPORTS  - FOR THIS TASK TRUVEN HEALTH WILL LEAD WORK EFFORTS, AS STATED ABOVE, INCLUDING ANALYSES, PRESENTING FINDINGS TO THE INTERAGENCY WORK GROUP AS REQUESTED, AND CONDUCT FURTHER DISSEMINATION AS AGREED UPON WITH STANFORD AND AHRQ. TASK 5: MONITOR EFFECTIVE STRATEGIES FOR REDUCING MEDICAL ERRORS AND INCREASING PATIENT SAFETY - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL CONSULT ON THE WORK PLAN AND REVIEW WORK MATERIALS. TASK 6: DISSEMINATE FINDINGS FROM ANALYSES -  FOR THIS TASK TRUVEN HEALTH WILL CREATE THE DISSEMINATION PLAN. TRUVEN HEALTH WILL PROVIDE TWO INDIVIDUALS TO ATTEND THE PSO ANNUAL MEETING, AND CREATE 2 EDUCATIONAL BRIEFS. TASK 7: ADMINISTER TASK ORDER - THE CONTRACTOR SHALL DELIVER A MONTHLY PROGRESS REPORT TO THE STANFORD. OPTIONAL TASK 8: ASSESS FEASIBILITY OF THE CREATION OF AN INTERACTIVE EVIDENCE-BASED MANAGEMENT RESOURCE FOR NETWORK OF PATIENT SAFETY DATABASES - FOR THIS TASK, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL LEAD ALL WORK DESCRIBED ABOVE AND CREATE THE FINAL FEASIBILITY REPORT.  OPTIONAL TASK 9: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS - OPTIONAL TASK 9A: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE 500 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 6 MONTHS. THIS OPTIONAL TASK WILL BE AWARDED ON A TIME AND MATERIALS BASIS TO PRODUCE 500 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLETED RESULTS. OPTIONAL TASK 9B: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE 750 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 6 MONTHS. THIS OPTIONAL TASK WILL BE AWARDED ON A TIME AND MATERIALS BASIS TO PRODUCE 750 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLETED RESULTS. OPTIONAL TASK 9C: ANALYZE NON-IDENTIFIABLE PSO DATA Â€“ PRODUCE 1000 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLET RESULTS PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: 6 MONTHS. THIS OPTIONAL TASK WILL BE AWARDED ON A TIME AND MATERIALS BASIS TO PRODUCE 1000 ADDITIONAL TABLES AND BULLETED RESULTS. FOR EACH OF THE OPTION 9A-9C, TRUVEN HEALTH WILL CREATE 50% OF THE TABLES AND ASSOCIATED DOCUMENTATION.
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality

Sub-Award Description: OFFICE OF THE DIRECTOR, DIVISION OF PROGRAM COORDINATION AND PLANNING AND STRATEGIC INITIATIVES - SUBCONTRACTOR WILL PROVIDE SUPPORT TO OFFICE OF PORTFOLIO ANALYSIS (OPA) IN THE DEVELOPMENT, ASSESSMENT AND MODIFICATION OF A VARIETY OF ANALYTICAL TOOLS AND SUPPORT FOR THE RETRIEVAL, MANIPULATION AND EVALUATION OF COMPLEX TEXT-BASED BIOMEDICAL DATA; WORK WITH EXPERT STAFF IN SCIENCE PORTFOLIO ANALYSIS TO ENHANCE THE EXISTING TOOL SET; IDENTIFY, EVALUATE AND MODIFY NEW OPEN SOURCE TOOLS; DEVELOP PATCHES, ROUTINES, SCRIPTS AND QUERIES IN SUPPORT OF ANALYTICS; CONTRIBUTE IN A COMPUTER LABORATORY ENVIRONMENT WITH WINDOWS, UNIX AND LINUX DEVELOPMENT AND TEST ENVIRONMENTS; AND WORK WITH THE OPA TEAM TO ACCESS NIH STRUCTURED DATA (E.G., DATABASES), UNSTRUCTURED DATA (E.G., SCIENTIFIC LITERATURE, GRANT PROPOSALS, ETC.) AND PERFORM DATABASE FUNCTIONS FOR DATA WAREHOUSING, DATA MINING, TEXT MINING, NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING, VISUAL DATA ANALYSIS AND NETWORK ANALYSIS.
Awarding Agency: Department of Health and Human Services
Awarding Sub Agency: National Institutes of Health
